state_program_name: Home Services Agency license (IDPH) under the Home Health, Home Services, and Home Nursing Agency Licensing Act (210 ILCS 55; 77 Ill. Adm. Code 245). Non-medical in-home services paid privately, or through the IDoA Community Care Program and the DHS-DRS Home Services Program.

front_matter.purpose:
## Purpose

This Policy & Procedure Manual sets out how **[AGENCY NAME]** delivers non-medical in-home services in Illinois. It is written to meet the Illinois Department of Public Health (IDPH) licensing requirements for a **Home Services Agency** under the Home Health, Home Services, and Home Nursing Agency Licensing Act (210 ILCS 55) and the Home Health, Home Services, and Home Nursing Agency Code (77 Ill. Adm. Code 245).

The manual does four things:

- It gives the governing body, the Agency Manager, supervisors, and in-home services workers one written source of agency policy and procedure. This supports the safe and adequate care that 77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.30(b) requires.
- It supplies the written policies IDPH asks to see with an initial Home Services Application (IDPH Form 445104) and later at survey.
- It states plainly what workers may and may not do. Services are limited to non-medical help: activities of daily living (ADLs), personal care, medication reminding, housekeeping, laundry, meal preparation, shopping, transportation to appointments, and companionship. Nothing that requires a license under the Nurse Practice Act is permitted, and medication setup is prohibited.
- It protects clients by setting standards for client agreements, service plans, records, confidentiality, complaints, infection control, and the prevention and reporting of abuse, neglect, and financial exploitation.

**Service model.** Before adoption, [AGENCY NAME] must state in Section 1 whether it operates as a **direct-service (employer) agency** or as a **home services placement agency**. The placement-agency rules in 77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.214 apply only to placement agencies. A placement agency may not be the worker's employer, may not direct or supervise the worker, and may charge only a one-time placement fee. The rest of this manual is written for a direct-service agency, and any placement-agency variations are flagged where they occur.

**Payer sources.** Licensed home services agencies serve clients who pay privately or through private insurance. Medicaid-funded clients are served through the IDoA Community Care Program (CCP) or the DHS-DRS Home Services Program. Under 77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.20, a program that serves clients *exclusively* through IDoA CCP, the DHS Office of Rehabilitation Services, or the VA is not a home services agency. Agencies that serve those programs should confirm their licensure status with IDPH.
front_matter.how_to_use:
## How to Use This Manual

**Customize it first.** This manual is a template. Replace every **[AGENCY NAME]** placeholder and every bracketed item with the agency's actual name, titles, contact numbers, hours of operation, service list, counties served, and the choice of service model (direct-service or placement). Delete or revise any text that does not describe what the agency really does. Policies that are never followed will cause survey problems.

**Adopt it formally.** Under 77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.30(a), the governing body must adopt and revise the agency's operating policies and procedures, meet to review agency operations, and keep minutes of all meetings. Record adoption of this manual, and every later revision, in the governing body's minutes. Complete the adoption page and keep the signed copy with the minutes.

**Keep it current.**
- The governing body's bylaws (or equivalent) must be reviewed annually and revised as needed (245.30(a)). Review this manual on the same schedule.
- The quality improvement program evaluates the agency's total program at least once a year (245.240(a)). Use its findings to update policies.
- Revise the manual whenever Part 245, the Act, or IDPH guidance changes. The Agency Manager must know the Department's rules and keep them in the agency (245.40(a)).
- Log each revision with its date, what changed, and the date of governing body approval.
- Notify IDPH of agency changes within 10 days, using the Facility Information Change Form. The agency also needs IDPH approval before serving a new county (IDPH Home Services Agencies FAQ).

**Train staff on it.** The Agency Manager must familiarize employees with the Act and the rules and provide orientation and in-service education (245.40(a)). Every worker must complete the training required by 245.71, with documentation. Give each employee access to this manual, and give a signed acknowledgment of receipt and training to be kept in the personnel file. Re-train staff whenever a policy changes materially.

**Find your way around.**
- Sections follow the order of IDPH's initial-applicant policy checklist, so each topic is easy to find at application and at survey.
- Each policy cites the section of 77 Ill. Adm. Code 245 that it implements.
- **Appendix A** maps every item on the official IDPH checklist to the policy in this manual that satisfies it. Use it to check completeness before submitting an application and to show a surveyor where each required policy is located.
- Keep a copy of the manual in the agency office. Records must stay confidential, and the office must have a working telephone staffed during business hours (245.40(a)).

**Verify the full rule text.** Some rule subsections were only partly available when this manual was prepared. Before finalizing, read the full current text of Part 245 on the JCAR website for these items: 245.40(c)(4)(M)-(P); 245.40(c)(6)(B), including the routine supervisory visit interval; 245.75(b); 245.240(b); and the minimum liability insurance limits under 245.90(a). Do not rely on secondary sources for these.
front_matter.regulatory_framework:
## Regulatory Framework

### Governing statutes and rules

The following are the rules this manual implements. Cites are given as they appear in the source citations.

**Licensing statute and code**
- **210 ILCS 55**, Home Health, Home Services, and Home Nursing Agency Licensing Act. No one may open, manage, conduct, or maintain a home services agency without an IDPH license.
- **77 Ill. Adm. Code 245**, Home Health, Home Services, and Home Nursing Agency Code. Subpart A, General (245.10-245.25); Subpart B, Operational Requirements (245.30-245.75); Subpart C, Licensure Procedures (245.80-245.150); Subpart D, Client/Patient Services (245.200-245.250). The most recent amendment shown is 49 Ill. Reg. 4661, effective 3/25/2025.

**Organization, administration, and personnel**
- **77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.20**, Definitions (including the exclusion of programs serving clients exclusively through IDoA CCP, DHS Office of Rehabilitation Services, or the VA, and the definition of "client record").
- **77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.30(a)**, governing body, bylaws, adoption of policies, minutes.
- **77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.30(b)(1)-(3)**, written administrative policies, liability insurance, complaint resolution.
- **77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.30(c)(1)(A)-(I)**, personnel policies.
- **77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.30(c)(2)-(5)**, license verification, personnel records, contracted staff.
- **77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.30(f)(1)**, designation of the person who supervises services (Agency Manager).
- **77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.40(a)(1)-(13)**, Agency Manager responsibilities, office, operating hours.
- **77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.40(c)(1)-(3)**, home services worker definition and duties.
- **77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.40(c)(4)(A)-(L)**, acceptable tasks and limitations.
- **77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.40(c)(4)(N); 245.40(c)(5)(D)**, medication reminding; prohibition on medication setup.
- **77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.40(c)(6)**, supervision of a home services worker.

**Worker qualifications, training, and background checks**
- **77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.71(a)**, employment conditions.
- **77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.71(c)**, initial training.
- **77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.71(e)(1)-(14)**, required training subjects.
- **77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.71(f)**, annual training.
- **77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.71(g)-(i)**, supervisors/trainers and training documentation.
- **77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.72**, Health Care Worker Background Check.
- **225 ILCS 46; 77 Ill. Adm. Code 955**, Health Care Worker Background Check Act and Code.

**Infection control and health**
- **77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.75(a)**, infection control.
- **77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.55(a)**, vaccinations. These duties apply to home health and home nursing agencies, not to home services agencies, so this manual contains no client vaccination procedure.

**Client services**
- **77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.210(a)-(b)**, scope of services and contracted services.
- **77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.210(c)**, written client agreement.
- **77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.210(d)**, acceptance of clients and discharge.
- **77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.210(e)-(g)**, service plan.
- **77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.210(h)-(j)**, client records, retention, confidentiality.
- **77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.214**, home services placement agency (applies only if the agency uses the placement model).
- **77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.240(a)**, quality improvement program.
- **77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.250**, abuse, neglect, and financial exploitation prevention and reporting. Mandated-reporter duties under the Adult Protective Services Act (**320 ILCS 20**) remain in force.

**Licensure procedures**
- **77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.90(a)**, license application, including evidence of liability insurance.
- **77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.100**, provisional license (240 days, extendable 120 days with substantial progress).
- **77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.130(b)**, adverse licensure actions (an application not completed and approved within 90 days of submission may be denied).

**Agency guidance and payer program materials (not rules)**
- IDPH Home Services Agencies FAQ.
- IDPH Guidance for Common Deficiency Findings. This is survey guidance, not a rule. It covers annual Health Care Worker Registry verification and annual education, and the content required in training records.
- IDPH Home Services Application, Form 445104.
- HFS Electronic Visit Verification and the December 2025 Illinois EVV Updates (Medicaid personal care).
- IDoA Community Care Program current rates; DHS-DRS Home Services Program rates; HFS Persons who are Elderly HCBS waiver. These apply only if the agency participates in those programs.

### Regulators and contacts

| Regulator | Role | Contact |
|---|---|---|
| **Illinois Department of Public Health (IDPH), Home Services Program** | Licenses home services agencies: initial application, provisional license, surveys, county-expansion approval, change notices | 217-782-7412 (TTY 800-547-0466); DPH.COOS@illinois.gov; https://dph.illinois.gov/topics-services/health-care-regulation/health-care-facilities/home-services.html |
| **Illinois Department on Aging (IDoA), Community Care Program** | Operating agency for the Persons who are Elderly HCBS waiver; sets CCP in-home rates; Care Coordination Units assess and refer clients | Senior HelpLine 1-800-252-8966; https://ilaging.illinois.gov/programs/ccp/current-rates.html |
| **Illinois Department of Healthcare and Family Services (HFS)** | State Medicaid agency; HCBS waiver oversight; Electronic Visit Verification policy | https://hfs.illinois.gov/medicalclients/hcbs/elderly.html |
| **Illinois Department of Human Services, Division of Rehabilitation Services (DHS-DRS)** | Home Services Program for people with severe disabilities under age 60; sets HSP maximum unit prices | https://www.dhs.state.il.us/page.aspx?item=67182 |

Also keep on file the contact numbers for the following, as required by 245.250:
- the elder abuse provider agency designated by IDoA, or the Area Agency on Aging;
- the DCFS Child Abuse Hotline;
- local police and 911.

### Official review documents

IDPH has no separate policy-review checklist. It reviews an agency's policies through the application:

- **IDPH Form 445104, Home Services Application** (initial, renewal, and change of ownership), issued by the IDPH Health Care Facilities and Programs Section. The page titled "Required documentation to be provided with this application" contains the **"Initial Applicants ONLY" checklist**, which is the official policy checklist used to review this manual. The form footer reads "Updated 8/9/2023" on pp. 1-5 and "Updated 6/8/2023" on pp. 6-8, and the posted file is named hs-application-092024.pdf. Confirm on the IDPH website that you are using the current version. The form does not accept electronic submission; it is mailed to IDPH with the application fee.
- **77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.90(a)(3)(I)**, which requires copies of policies and procedures with the initial application, starting with complaint resolution (245.30(b)(3)) and employee health and safety (245.30(c)(1)(H) and (I)). It also requires client service contracts (245.220), acceptance criteria (245.210(d)), and sample service plan forms (245.210(e)).
- **IDPH Surveillance Nurse Visit Checklist (Home Services)**, which shows how surveyors review the manual on site. It covers policy and procedure manuals, bylaws, governing body minutes, complaint log and process, training files, job descriptions, service plans, and the Alzheimer's/dementia training curriculum. It is a survey tool and adds no new policy requirements.

**Appendix A maps every official item to the policy that satisfies it.** The checklist has no numbered items, so Appendix A uses the regulatory cite printed on each checklist line as the item ID and lists the manual section that meets it. The employee health and safety policy covers both 245.30(c)(1)(H) and (I). Items that are paperwork rather than policies are not mapped. These include forms, ownership and officer information, the fee, proof of liability coverage (245.90(a)(2)), proof of Health Care Worker Registry access (955.115), and the Attachment E manager qualification form. They must still be submitted with the application.

### Requirements for this manual

- **Customize.** Replace all [AGENCY NAME] placeholders and bracketed items so the manual reflects what the agency actually does.
- **Adopt.** The governing body must adopt the manual and any revisions and record them in its minutes (245.30(a)).
- **Keep current.** Review the manual at least annually and whenever the rules, IDPH guidance, or agency operations change. Keep a revision log.
- **Train.** Orient and train all staff on the manual, document the training, and keep signed acknowledgments in the personnel files (245.40(a); 245.71).

This manual is an operating tool and not legal advice. The Part 245 text on the JCAR website controls over any summary here.

citations.title: Home Health, Home Services, and Home Nursing Agency Licensing Act
citations.requirement: No one may open, manage, conduct or maintain a home services agency without an IDPH license. The Act is the enabling statute for 77 Ill. Adm. Code 245. (From the fact-checked research; Act text not re-fetched.)

citations.title: Home Health, Home Services, and Home Nursing Agency Code
citations.requirement: Part 245 has four subparts: A General (245.10-245.25), B Operational Requirements (245.30-245.75), C Licensure Procedures (245.80-245.150), D Client/Patient Services (245.200-245.250). Section titles were confirmed from the table of contents. Most recent amendment shown: 49 Ill. Reg. 4661, eff. 3/25/2025.

citations.title: Definitions
citations.requirement: Programs serving clients exclusively through IDoA CCP, DHS Office of Rehabilitation Services, or the VA are not home services agencies. 'Client record' means personal information, emergency notification information, agreed service plans, the home services contract, and documentation of services at each visit.

citations.title: Organization and Administration - Governing Body (all agencies)
citations.requirement: The agency must have a governing body with legal authority. The body must have bylaws or the equivalent, reviewed annually and revised as needed, that state the agency's objectives. It must adopt and revise operating policies and procedures, meet to review agency operations, and keep minutes of all meetings. The requirement to employ a qualified administrator is for home health agencies.

citations.title: Administration - all agencies
citations.requirement: The agency needs written administrative policies and procedures to ensure safe and adequate care. It must show evidence of liability insurance per 245.90(a). It must have written complaint-resolution policies between the agency and its clients and client advocates.

citations.title: Personnel policies - all agencies
citations.requirement: Written personnel policies must cover: (A) wage scales, benefits, hours and leave; (B) initial health evaluation of each new employee with client contact; (C) orientation and continuing education; (D) job descriptions for all positions; (E) annual performance evaluation; (F) Civil Rights Act of 1964 compliance; (G) confidentiality of personnel records; (H) employee health policy, including symptom and exposure reporting and removal from and return to client contact; (I) procedures for identifying and protecting staff from dangers in the home.

citations.title: Personnel - license verification, personnel records, contracted staff
citations.requirement: Before employing anyone in a position needing a State professional license, verify with IDFPR that the license is active and keep a copy in the personnel file. Personnel records must hold name and address, SSN, date of birth, next of kin, evidence of qualifications, employment dates, and the reason for separation. Home services agencies that use contracted services must ensure those workers hold any required license, registration or certification and are supervised by the agency.

citations.title: Agency Manager - Home Services and Home Nursing Agencies
citations.requirement: A home services agency must designate a person to supervise the provision of services (or oversee placement of workers). This is the verified designation rule. The research's reference to '245.40(f)' could not be confirmed and should not be used. No manager qualification list for home services agencies appears in 245.30(f) as fetched.

citations.title: Staffing - Administrator or Agency Manager responsibilities
citations.requirement: The manager must ensure legal compliance, know the Department's rules, keep them in the agency, and familiarize employees with the Act and rules. The manager keeps reports, records, personnel files and policies, maintains an organizational chart, hires per job descriptions, and provides orientation and in-service education. The manager must designate in writing a qualified person to act in the manager's absence. The agency must keep an office with a working telephone staffed during business hours. The office must protect record confidentiality and comply with fire-safety ordinances. The agency must adopt a written operating-hours policy that tells clients how to access care outside those hours.

citations.title: Home Services or In-Home Services Worker - definition and duties
citations.requirement: Home services means help with ADLs, housekeeping, personal laundry and companionship in the client's residence. It excludes anything requiring a Nurse Practice Act licensee. Workers may observe and report changes in client functioning, do chores and meal preparation, help with shopping and appointments, provide companionship, document services, and assist with ADLs and personal care. Workers provide services only as Part 245 allows.

citations.title: Acceptable tasks and limitations (skin care through toileting)
citations.requirement: Task-by-task limits apply for skin care, ambulation, bathing, dressing/compression, exercise, feeding/thickener, hair care, mouth care, nail care, positioning, shaving and toileting. Most require three things: client or representative feedback, worker training in the method, and an agency competency evaluation. Several also require a health care professional's order. No passive range of motion, no nail trimming, and no skilled skin care. The fetched page was truncated after toileting (L), so the remaining items (M-P) must be read in full.

citations.title: Medication reminding; prohibited medication setup
citations.requirement: A worker may remind a client about medications only when they were pre-selected by the client, a family member, a nurse or a pharmacist and are in containers other than prescription bottles, such as medication minders. A worker may not perform or provide medication setup. Source: ilga.gov excerpts and the Illinois Register adoption text, seen in search results. Confirm the exact subsection wording in the full text.

citations.title: Supervision of a home services worker
citations.requirement: A supervisor must be designated and available to workers for questions at all times (not applicable to placement agencies). Supervisory visits must include an on-site visit within the next supervisory visit when an area of concern is noted. The supervisor must also make an annual on-site visit to observe and assess each worker giving care. The visit interval for routine supervision is not confirmed. A secondary source says 90 days; read the full text of (c)(6)(B) before publishing.

citations.title: Qualifications and Requirements for Home Services Workers - employment conditions
citations.requirement: For each worker who is not otherwise licensed, certified or registered, the agency must keep in the employee file documentation of: (1) no disqualifying Health Care Worker Background Check without a waiver; (2) a copy of the Social Security card; (3) a visa or proof of citizenship that meets federal employment requirements.

citations.title: Initial training - home services agency
citations.requirement: The agency must provide or arrange at least 10 hours of initial training per worker. Five hours must come before the first assignment, and the other 5 within 30 days of the start of employment. The agency may accept proof of training from another licensed home services agency within the prior 365 days, including a CNA on the Health Care Worker Registry. Such workers still get a competency evaluation before their first assignment. No assignment may be given until the worker passes a competency evaluation on the first 5 hours of topics, with a second test after the remaining 5 hours. (The 8-hour figure in 245.71(b) and 245.214(e) applies only to placement agencies.)

citations.title: Required training subjects
citations.requirement: Training must cover, in addition to 245.40(c)(4)(A)-(P): job responsibilities and limits; communication with people who are hard of hearing or have dementia; observing, reporting and documenting; personal care tasks including medication reminding; adaptive equipment; hygiene and infection control; a clean and safe environment; safety precautions; emergencies, first aid and the client's emergency preparedness plan; confidentiality; understanding dementia; problem-solving for challenging dementia behaviors; abuse and neglect and reporting duties; and any other task the agency assigns.

citations.title: Annual training
citations.requirement: Every worker needs at least 10 hours of training per year of employment, on a calendar-year or anniversary basis chosen by the agency. The initial 10 hours satisfy the first year. Self-study with demonstrated learning is allowed. Annual training must include: client dignity, independence, self-determination, privacy, choice and rights; disaster procedures; hygiene and infection control; abuse and neglect prevention and reporting; and the ADL tasks in 245.40(c)(4)(A)-(P), including oxygen delivery for workers who serve clients on oxygen.

citations.title: Supervisors/trainers and training documentation
citations.requirement: The agency must have home services supervisors or trainers who give initial training and ongoing supervision. Each must either (1) have at least 2 years of qualifying experience within the last 5 years, or (2) hold a current supervisory or trainer position and have had training within the past year on the permitted tasks, provided by or developed by a qualified professional. Supervisors and trainers must be available to workers for continuing education. All training must be documented with date, minutes per topic, instructor and qualifications, content description, and worker signature or electronic certificate with date/time stamp.

citations.title: Health Care Worker Background Check
citations.requirement: An agency must comply with the Health Care Worker Background Check Act (225 ILCS 46) and the Health Care Worker Background Check Code (77 Ill. Adm. Code 955).

citations.title: Health Care Worker Background Check Act and Code
citations.requirement: Fingerprint-based checks are required for covered workers. Fingerprints are sent to the Illinois State Police within 10 working days (per the research). Results initiated through IDPH are entered in the Health Care Worker Registry. The application package requires proof of access to the IDPH Registry (955.115, per Form 445104).

citations.title: Infection Control
citations.requirement: Each agency must develop and implement policies and procedures for investigating, controlling and preventing infections. The requirement for placement agencies to give workers the CDC hand-hygiene guideline does not apply to a direct-service agency. Subsection (b), on adherence to CDC guidance, was only partly visible; read it in full.

citations.title: Vaccinations (scope)
citations.requirement: Influenza and pneumococcal vaccination duties apply to home health agencies and home nursing agencies, not to home services agencies. Do not write client vaccination procedures for this license.

citations.title: Services - Home Services Agencies: scope and contracted services
citations.requirement: A home services agency provides non-medical services, directly or by contract, such as ADL support, personal care, medication reminding, housekeeping, laundry, cooking, shopping, transport to appointments, household records and companionship. The agency must keep a list of services offered and the scope of work for each. It must give that list to clients before contracting, with the signed contract, and whenever it changes. Contracts with third-party providers must be written and include 9 elements: services, adherence to agency policies and personnel requirements, agency control, notes, charges, liability and insurance, term, signatures, and termination.

citations.title: Written client agreement
citations.requirement: A written client agreement must include: (1) assurance of compliance with the Act, including the Health Care Worker Background Check Act; (2) who pays employment taxes, Social Security taxes and workers' compensation; (3) who supervises workers and who hires, fires and disciplines them; (4) charges, payment schedule and payee; (5) contract term and termination conditions; (6) contact information for concerns, complaints and questions.

citations.title: Acceptance of clients; discharge
citations.requirement: The agency must develop and follow written acceptance and discharge policies. Acceptance is based on need for non-medical help, and the agency may not provide medical services. A totally dependent repositioning client may be accepted only if the worker is trained and competency-evaluated and the representative can assist or give feedback. No one may be refused service on the basis of the protected classes listed in 775 ILCS 5/1-103(Q). Termination requires at least 7 working days' written notice with a stated reason, kept in the record. The 7-day notice does not apply when worker safety is at risk, and the risk must be documented. Acceptance must be based on documented functional limitations and relevant circumstances, including basic information on medications, treatments, activity, diet and mental status.

citations.title: Service plan
citations.requirement: A plan is required for every client, developed with agency staff, the client or representative or POA, and family if the client wishes. It must cover ADL and in-home support, medication reminders (frequency and time of day), treatments being received, activity, diet, functional limitations and essential procedures, mental health status, frequency of visits, equipment, and client limitations. It may not include tasks outside the worker scope in 245.40(c)(4). No physician signature is required. Review and revise as needed, and at least annually.

citations.title: Client records, retention, confidentiality
citations.requirement: Each client record must hold identifying information, representative contact information, an emergency contact, the agreed service plan, the signed home care services agreement, and worker documentation of each service at each visit. A written records policy is required. Records must be kept at least 2 years after the last date of service, in hard copy or electronic form. Faxed copies must be on non-thermal paper. A written confidentiality policy must cover use, removal and release of records.

citations.title: Quality Improvement Program
citations.requirement: Home nursing, home services and placement agencies must develop a quality improvement program with written policies. The program must evaluate the agency's total program at least once a year. Subsection (b) requires record review. Its detail, and the content of the evaluation for home services agencies, was not retrieved; read in full.

citations.title: Abuse, Neglect and Financial Exploitation Prevention and Reporting
citations.requirement: On reasonable suspicion of abuse, neglect or financial exploitation of a client aged 60+, a disabled client, or any 'eligible adult' under the Adult Protective Services Act (320 ILCS 20), notify the elder abuse provider agency designated by IDoA or the Area Agency on Aging. For a victim under 18, call the DCFS Child Abuse Hotline. Document each report and keep it on premises for 12 months. If an employee is the alleged perpetrator, remove them from direct client contact immediately and investigate. Complete a written investigation report within 14 days of the initial report. Send it to IDPH within 24 hours after the investigation is completed and keep a copy for 12 months. The report must contain the six elements in (d). Employees and volunteers must report to management and to the elder abuse provider agency or IDoA. Call 911 or local police immediately for staff-inflicted physical injury, sexual abuse by staff, a crime in the home by another person, or a death other than by disease or natural causes. A written law-enforcement notification policy is required. Mandated-reporter duties under 320 ILCS 20 remain.

citations.title: Services - Home Services Placement Agency
citations.requirement: A placement agency may not be the employer, may not direct or supervise the worker, and may charge only a one-time placement fee. It must identify itself as a placement agency in all marketing. This section does not apply to a direct-service (employer) agency; the manual should state which model the agency uses.

citations.title: License Application - evidence of liability insurance
citations.requirement: The agency must show evidence of liability insurance. The 245.30(b)(2) text confirms the cross-reference. The minimum limits were not confirmed; a secondary source says $1M per occurrence and $3M aggregate, which is unverified.

citations.title: Provisional License
citations.requirement: Provisional license valid 240 days, extendable 120 days with substantial progress. The full home services license expires one year from the end of the month the provisional license was first issued. (From the fact-checked research.)

citations.title: Adverse Licensure Actions - application not completed within 90 days
citations.requirement: An application not completed and approved within 90 days of submission may be denied (as cited by IDPH; from the research).

citations.title: Home Services Agencies Frequently Asked Questions
citations.requirement: Licensees take private pay or private insurance. Medicaid clients are served through IDoA CCP or DHS-DRS. IDPH does an initial application review within 30 days. A compliance survey takes place within 30 days of provisional license expiration. The agency needs IDPH approval before serving a new county. The agency must notify IDPH within 10 days of any change, using the Facility Information Change Form. (From the research.)

citations.cite: IDPH Guidance for Common Deficiency Findings
citations.title: Common Survey Deficiencies - annual registry verification and education
citations.requirement: Surveyors cite 245.71 (home services only) and 973.140 for training deficiencies. The guidance covers annual Health Care Worker Registry verification and annual education. Training records must show date, minutes per topic, instructor and qualifications, content and worker signature. This is survey guidance, not a rule.

citations.title: Home Services Application
citations.requirement: The application requires: complaint-resolution policy; employee health and safety policy; infection control policy; background-check process; supervisory-visit policies; employee training procedure (245.71); sample service plan; job descriptions; and proof of IDPH Registry access. A $1,500 fee by check or money order is due with the application. The form has an 'Alternate Agency Manager' line. (From the research.)

citations.cite: HFS Electronic Visit Verification; December 2025 Illinois EVV Updates
citations.title: Illinois EVV for Medicaid personal care
citations.requirement: Personal care and home health EVV data is integrated in HHAeXchange from March 2, 2026. HFS requires at least 75% quarterly EVV compliance from April 1, 2026. The state EVV solution is free to providers. (From the research.)

citations.cite: IDoA Community Care Program current rates (eff. 1/1/2026)
citations.title: CCP in-home service rate S5130
citations.requirement: CCP in-home service (S5130) is $30.80/hour statewide, or $32.57/hour with insurance. IDoA is the operating agency, and Care Coordination Units assess and refer clients. Senior HelpLine 1-800-252-8966 is for client applications. (From the research.)

citations.title: HSP maximum unit prices
citations.requirement: Homemaker (4100) $30.80/hour; personal assistant (4150) $20.00/hour; non-agency CNA (4198) $23.00/hour. HSP serves people with severe disabilities under age 60. (From the research.)

citations.cite: HFS Persons who are Elderly waiver
citations.title: Persons who are Elderly HCBS waiver
citations.requirement: HFS is the state Medicaid agency and IDoA is the operating agency for the Persons who are Elderly waiver. (From the research.)

policies.title: Organization, Governing Body and Agency Manager Responsibilities
policies.applies_to: Governing body, Agency Manager, Alternate Agency Manager and all supervisory staff
policies.purpose: To establish who holds legal authority over [AGENCY NAME], who is responsible for day-to-day supervision of services, and how those responsibilities continue when the manager is absent, as required for an Illinois Home Services Agency licensed by IDPH.
policies.policy:
[AGENCY NAME] is a direct-service (employer) home services agency. It employs, directs and supervises its own home services workers. It is not a home services placement agency and does not operate under the placement-agency model. [AGENCY NAME] operates only under a license issued by the Illinois Department of Public Health (IDPH) under the Home Health, Home Services, and Home Nursing Agency Licensing Act (210 ILCS 55) and 77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.

Governing body. [AGENCY NAME] has a governing body that holds legal authority over the agency. The governing body maintains bylaws or the equivalent that state the agency's objectives, and reviews them at least annually and revises them as needed. The governing body adopts and revises the agency's operating policies and procedures, meets to review agency operations, and keeps minutes of all meetings (77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.30(a)).

Agency Manager. [AGENCY NAME] designates a person to supervise the provision of services and to oversee the assignment of workers (77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.30(f)(1)). That person is the Agency Manager, [ADMINISTRATOR NAME]. The Agency Manager carries out the duties listed in 77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.40(a): ensuring legal compliance; knowing the Department's rules and keeping them in the agency; familiarizing employees with the Act and rules; keeping reports, records, personnel files and policies; maintaining an organizational chart; hiring according to job descriptions; and providing orientation and in-service education.

Absence coverage. The Agency Manager designates in writing a qualified person to act in the manager's absence. That person is the Alternate Agency Manager, [ALTERNATE MANAGER NAME]. The same person is named on the Alternate Agency Manager line of IDPH Form 445104.

definitions.definition: The owner(s), board or other group with legal authority over [AGENCY NAME] that adopts policies, reviews operations and is accountable for the agency's compliance.
The person designated to supervise the provision of home services and to oversee placement of workers. For this agency the title is Agency Manager.
The qualified person designated in writing to act when the Agency Manager is absent.
An agency that employs and supervises its own workers, as opposed to a placement agency, which may not be the employer and may not direct or supervise the worker.
77 Ill. Adm. Code 245, the IDPH rules for home health, home services and home nursing agencies.

procedures: The governing body adopts written bylaws (or the equivalent) that state the agency's objectives. The Agency Manager files the signed bylaws in the governing body records binder.
The governing body reviews the bylaws at least once every calendar year. It records any revisions, the review date and the approver in the minutes.

The governing body meets at least [FREQUENCY, e.g., quarterly] to review agency operations. The agenda covers complaints, incidents, quality improvement results, staffing, training compliance and survey activity.

The designated recorder takes minutes of every governing body meeting. The minutes show the date, attendees, topics, decisions and votes. The Agency Manager files them within 10 business days of the meeting.
The governing body adopts and revises operating policies and procedures by recorded vote. It follows the process in GOV-03 for each adoption or revision.

The governing body designates the Agency Manager in writing. The designation states the name, start date and the duty to supervise services and oversee worker placement. The Agency Manager signs to accept.
The Agency Manager designates the Alternate Agency Manager in writing, signed and dated by both. The Agency Manager gives a copy to the governing body and files one in the administrative records.
The Alternate Agency Manager's authority covers all Agency Manager duties during any absence. The Agency Manager tells all staff who the alternate is and how to reach that person.

The Agency Manager keeps a complete, current copy of the Act (210 ILCS 55) and Part 245 at the agency office, printed or readily accessible electronically. The Agency Manager checks IDPH's website at least [FREQUENCY, e.g., quarterly] for amendments and brings changes to the governing body.
The Agency Manager familiarizes each new employee with the Act and rules during orientation (see PER-03). Employees acknowledge this in writing.

The Agency Manager maintains a current organizational chart showing the governing body, Agency Manager, Alternate Agency Manager, supervisors, office staff and home services workers. The Agency Manager updates it within 10 days of any change in these positions and files each version with its date.
The Agency Manager keeps the agency's reports, client records, personnel files and policies in the secured office. Access is limited as described in CR-03 and REC-02.
The Agency Manager hires only according to written job descriptions (PER-10) and arranges orientation and in-service education (PER-03 and PER-05).

If the Agency Manager position becomes vacant, the governing body names a replacement in writing as soon as possible. Until then the Alternate Agency Manager acts. The governing body then notifies IDPH as described in GOV-07.
The Agency Manager reports to the governing body at each meeting on compliance status, open corrective actions and any survey findings.

responsibilities.duty: Holds legal authority; reviews bylaws annually; adopts and revises policies; meets to review operations; keeps minutes; designates the Agency Manager.

Supervises services and oversees worker placement; ensures legal compliance; keeps the Act, Part 245, records, personnel files, policies and organizational chart; hires per job descriptions; provides orientation and in-service education; designates an alternate in writing.
Acts with full manager authority during the manager's absence and reports actions taken on return.
Prepares and files minutes of all governing body meetings.

documentation: Bylaws (or equivalent) with annual review dates
Governing body meeting minutes
Written designation of the Agency Manager
Written designation of the Alternate Agency Manager
Organizational chart with revision dates
Copy of 210 ILCS 55 and 77 Ill. Adm. Code 245 kept at the office
Employee acknowledgments of the Act and rules

policies.title: Licensure, Service Area and Advertising Requirements
policies.applies_to: Governing body, Agency Manager, intake and marketing staff
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] holds a valid IDPH license at all times, serves clients only in counties IDPH has approved, and describes itself accurately in all advertising and marketing.
policies.policy:
No one may open, manage, conduct or maintain a home services agency in Illinois without an IDPH license (210 ILCS 55). [AGENCY NAME] does not accept clients, schedule workers or advertise services until IDPH has issued its license.

Application. [AGENCY NAME] applies on IDPH Home Services Application, Form 445104. The non-refundable $1,500 fee is paid by check or money order and is submitted with the application. The application includes the complaint-resolution policy, employee health and safety policy, infection control policy, background-check process, supervisory-visit policies, employee training procedure, sample service plan, job descriptions, proof of IDPH Health Care Worker Registry access, and evidence of liability insurance (77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.90(a)). IDPH does an initial review of an application within 30 days of submission. An application not completed and approved within 90 days of submission may be denied (77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.130(b)). [AGENCY NAME] therefore responds to IDPH requests for information promptly and completely.

Provisional and full license. A provisional license is valid for 240 days and may be extended 120 days if the agency shows substantial progress. IDPH conducts a compliance survey within 30 days of provisional license expiration. The full license expires one year from the end of the month in which the provisional license was first issued (77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.100). [AGENCY NAME] tracks these dates and files renewal on time.

Service area. [AGENCY NAME] serves only counties approved by IDPH. IDPH approval is obtained before the agency accepts any client in a new county (see GOV-07).

Payer model. [AGENCY NAME] serves private-pay and private-insurance clients. Medicaid-eligible clients are served through the IDoA Community Care Program (CCP) or the DHS-DRS Home Services Program (HSP) (see SVC-13).

Advertising. [AGENCY NAME] advertises only as a licensed home services agency offering non-medical in-home services. Because [AGENCY NAME] is a direct-service employer agency, the placement-agency identification requirement (77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.214) does not apply. The agency never describes itself as a placement agency, never charges a one-time placement fee in place of its service rates, and never advertises services outside its license or approved counties.

definitions.definition: Non-medical, in-home assistance such as homemaker and personal care services, as defined in the Act and Part 245 and limited by SVC-01.
The initial license issued by IDPH, valid 240 days and extendable 120 days if the agency shows substantial progress.
The Illinois counties IDPH has approved [AGENCY NAME] to serve.
An agency that refers workers but is not their employer and does not direct or supervise them. [AGENCY NAME] is not a placement agency.
The IDPH Home Services Application used for initial, renewal and change-of-ownership applications.

procedures: The Agency Manager completes IDPH Form 445104 in full, including the Alternate Agency Manager line, and has the governing body review it before submission.

The Agency Manager attaches every required item: complaint-resolution policy (CR-02), employee health and safety policy (PER-08), infection control policy (SAF-04), background-check process (PER-02), supervisory-visit policies (SVC-04 and SVC-05), employee training procedure (PER-03 through PER-06), sample service plan (SVC-03), job descriptions (PER-10), proof of Registry access, and evidence of liability insurance (GOV-09).

The Agency Manager submits the $1,500 fee by check or money order only, since electronic payment is not accepted. The Agency Manager records the check number and date, and notes that the fee is non-refundable.
The Agency Manager records the submission date and calendar-tracks the 30-day IDPH review date and the 90-day completion deadline.
The Agency Manager answers every IDPH request for information within [NUMBER] business days, or sooner if IDPH sets an earlier date. Each response is logged.

On receiving the provisional license, the Agency Manager records the issue date and calculates three dates: day 240 expiration, the possible 120-day extension, and the full license expiration (one year from the end of the month of first provisional issuance).

The Agency Manager conducts an internal readiness review at least 60 days before the provisional license expires, covering policies, training records, Registry verifications and client records (see GOV-06).
If the agency will need an extension, the Agency Manager documents its substantial progress and asks IDPH for the extension before the 240 days run out.
The agency does not accept clients, assign workers or advertise until the IDPH license is in hand. The Agency Manager keeps the license on file and posts a copy at the office.
The Agency Manager lists the approved counties in the licensing file. Intake staff check a prospective client's county against this list before any assessment or acceptance (SVC-02).

For any county not on the approved list, the Agency Manager follows GOV-07 and obtains IDPH approval before accepting a client there. Intake staff refer callers in unapproved counties to other resources and document the referral.

Before use, the Agency Manager reviews every advertisement, website page, brochure, social media post and directory listing. Each must state that [AGENCY NAME] is a licensed home services agency providing non-medical services, and may not claim nursing or medical care.
No marketing may call [AGENCY NAME] a placement agency or imply that workers are independent contractors referred by the agency.
Marketing may describe Medicaid access only as available through IDoA CCP or DHS-DRS HSP, with eligibility determined by those programs.
The Agency Manager keeps a dated copy of each approved advertisement for at least [NUMBER] years and reviews all advertising at least annually.
The Agency Manager submits the license renewal application and the $1,500 fee well before the expiration date, and files a copy of the renewed license.

responsibilities.duty: Authorizes the application and fee; ensures the agency operates only under a valid license.
Prepares and submits Form 445104; tracks provisional, survey, expiration and renewal dates; approves advertising; maintains the approved-county list.
Verify the client's county against the approved list before acceptance; use only approved marketing language.
Submit all materials to the Agency Manager for approval before publication.

documentation: Completed Form 445104 and all attachments
Fee check or money order record
IDPH correspondence log
Provisional and full licenses
License date tracker (240-day, extension, survey window, expiration)
Approved-county list and IDPH county approvals
Approved advertising file with dates

policies.title: Policy Review and Document Control
policies.applies_to: Governing body, Agency Manager and all staff who use the Policy & Procedure Manual
policies.purpose: To make sure the agency's written policies are adopted by the governing body, reviewed at least annually, revised when needed, and available to all staff in their current form.
policies.policy: The governing body adopts and revises the agency's operating policies and procedures (77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.30(a)). [AGENCY NAME] maintains written administrative policies and procedures that ensure safe and adequate care (77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.30(b)). The bylaws are reviewed annually. The Policy & Procedure Manual is reviewed at least annually, and every adoption, revision and review is recorded in the governing body minutes with the date and approver. Only the current version is in use, and staff are told about each change.

definitions.definition: The agency's complete set of written operating policies and procedures.
The current, approved version of a policy, bearing its effective date and version number.
The log showing each policy's version number, change summary, approval date and approver.

procedures: The governing body adopts the initial manual by recorded vote. The minutes list each policy ID and title adopted and the effective date.
Each policy carries a header with its ID, title, version number, effective date and the date of the last review.
The Agency Manager keeps a master revision log listing every policy, its current version, effective date, last review date and next review date.
The Agency Manager reviews every policy at least once every 12 months and sets the review calendar at the start of each year.

The Agency Manager also triggers an immediate review when any of the following occurs: a change to the Act or Part 245; an IDPH survey finding; a change in IDoA, HFS or DHS-DRS requirements; a quality improvement finding; or a serious incident.
The Agency Manager prepares proposed revisions in tracked form with a short summary of the reason for each change.
The governing body reviews and approves the revisions by recorded vote. The minutes record the policy ID, the revision date and the approver's name.
The Agency Manager updates the version number, effective date and revision log within 5 business days of approval.
The Agency Manager replaces the controlled copies in the office and the electronic manual. Outdated versions are marked superseded and archived, and they are not discarded.

The Agency Manager tells all affected staff of each change within 10 days of the effective date. Where the change affects client care, staff are re-trained, and signed acknowledgments are filed in personnel records.
New employees receive the manual or the policies relevant to their job during orientation and sign an acknowledgment (PER-03).
The governing body reviews the bylaws once a year and records the review in the minutes.
The Agency Manager keeps superseded policies for at least [NUMBER] years so the policy in force on any past date can be shown to a surveyor.
The Agency Manager reports at each governing body meeting on policies reviewed, policies overdue and changes proposed.

responsibilities.duty: Adopts and revises policies by recorded vote; reviews the bylaws annually; records approvals in minutes.
Maintains the manual, revision log and review calendar; drafts revisions; distributes updates; keeps archives.
Follow the current policies; sign acknowledgments; raise suggestions or conflicts with the Agency Manager.

documentation: Governing body minutes recording adoption, revision, review date and approver
Master revision log
Controlled copies with version and effective dates
Archive of superseded policies
Staff acknowledgments of policy changes
Annual bylaws review record

policies.title: Quality Improvement Program
policies.applies_to: Governing body, Agency Manager, supervisors and all staff
policies.purpose: To set up a written quality improvement (QI) program that evaluates the agency's total program at least once a year and drives corrective action.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] maintains a written quality improvement program, as required for home services agencies by 77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.240(a). The program evaluates the agency's total program at least once a year. The evaluation includes the record review required by 77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.240(b). The Agency Manager has read Section 245.240 in full and will align this policy with its detailed requirements. The agency reviews complaints, incidents, missed visits, supervisory-visit findings and training completion, and uses the results to improve services. Results are reported to the governing body.

definitions.definition: The agency's written, ongoing process for measuring its services, identifying problems and acting on them.
A yearly review of all parts of the agency's operation, including services, records, personnel and policies.
A structured review of a sample of client records, using a written audit tool, to check completeness and compliance.
A written plan that states the problem, the actions to correct it, the person responsible and the due date.

procedures: The governing body approves this QI policy and names the Agency Manager as QI coordinator.
The Agency Manager sets an annual QI calendar at the start of each year, showing quarterly data reviews and the annual total program evaluation date.

Each quarter, the Agency Manager compiles data on: complaints received and outcomes (CR-02); incidents and injuries (SAF-03); missed or late visits (SVC-09); supervisory-visit findings for clients and workers (SVC-04 and SVC-05); and training completion and annual Registry verification (PER-05 and PER-06).
For Medicaid-funded services, the Agency Manager also reviews EVV compliance against the 75% quarterly threshold HFS requires from April 1, 2026 (SVC-10).

At least quarterly, the Agency Manager audits a sample of client records and of personnel and training records using the written audit tool. The audit checks the records required by REC-01, REC-04 and PER-11. The sample size is [NUMBER] or [PERCENT] of active records, whichever is greater.
The Agency Manager documents each finding, its cause and trends, with dates and the staff involved.
For each finding, the Agency Manager writes a corrective action plan with the action, responsible person and due date, and follows up until it is closed.

Once a year, the Agency Manager completes a written evaluation of the agency's total program covering governance, services, client rights, personnel, records and QI results. The evaluation states which goals were met and which were not.
The Agency Manager presents the quarterly data and the annual evaluation to the governing body. The minutes record the discussion and any decisions.
The governing body sets QI goals for the next year and approves needed policy changes (GOV-03).
The Agency Manager shares QI results and changes with staff in meetings or written notices within 30 days.
The Agency Manager keeps all QI records, including audit tools, data summaries, corrective action plans and annual evaluations, for at least [NUMBER] years and makes them available to IDPH surveyors.

responsibilities.duty: Approves the QI program; reviews results; sets goals and resources.
Runs the QI calendar; collects data; audits records; writes corrective action plans; completes the annual evaluation.
Supply supervisory-visit findings, missed visit data and incident data; carry out corrective actions.
Report problems and cooperate with audits and corrective actions.

documentation: Written QI program and annual QI calendar
Quarterly data summaries
Record audit tools and completed audits
Corrective action plans and closure records
Annual total program evaluation
Governing body minutes showing QI review

policies.title: Corporate Compliance, Fraud and Billing Integrity
policies.applies_to: Governing body, Agency Manager, billing staff, supervisors and all home services workers
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] bills only for services actually delivered and documented, follows payer rules, and gives staff a safe way to report billing concerns.
policies.policy:
[AGENCY NAME] is licensed to serve private-pay and private-insurance clients. Medicaid clients are served through the IDoA Community Care Program (CCP) or the DHS-DRS Home Services Program (HSP). IDoA is the operating agency for the Persons who are Elderly waiver, and HFS is the state Medicaid agency.

The agency bills only for visits actually delivered and documented. For Medicaid-funded services, billed time must match the Electronic Visit Verification (EVV) record. The agency uses the CCP in-home service rate (S5130, $30.80 per hour, or $32.57 per hour with insurance, effective 1/1/2026) and the HSP maximum unit prices (homemaker 4100 at $30.80 per hour; personal assistant 4150 at $20.00 per hour; non-agency CNA 4198 at $23.00 per hour, as updated 7/1/2026) only for services that the program has authorized. Rates are checked against the current published schedules.

Employees may report billing or compliance concerns confidentially, without fear of retaliation.

definitions.definition: Billing only for authorized services that were delivered and documented, at the correct rate and for the correct time.
An electronic record of the date, time, location and service of a visit. For Medicaid personal care, EVV data is integrated in HHAeXchange from March 2, 2026.
The IDoA Community Care Program, through which Care Coordination Units assess and refer eligible older adults.
The DHS-DRS Home Services Program for people with severe disabilities under age 60.
Knowingly billing for services not provided, inflating hours, billing unauthorized services or rates, falsifying records, or other misuse of payer funds.

procedures: The governing body names the Agency Manager as compliance officer. The governing body receives a compliance report at least [FREQUENCY, e.g., quarterly].

At orientation and annually, the Agency Manager trains all staff on this policy: what counts as fraud, how to document time accurately, and how to report concerns. Staff sign an acknowledgment, filed in personnel records.

Before service starts, billing staff confirm the payer: private pay, private insurance, CCP or HSP. For CCP or HSP, they confirm a current authorization from IDoA/the Care Coordination Unit or DHS-DRS that names the service, units and dates.

Billing staff set the billing rate from the signed service agreement (CR-06) for private clients, or from the current CCP or HSP published rate for program clients. The Agency Manager checks published rates at least every January and July and whenever a payer announces an update, and documents each check.
Workers document each visit as required by REC-04 and, for Medicaid-funded services, record start and end times through the EVV system (SVC-10).
Before each billing cycle, billing staff compare the time sheets, visit notes and EVV data for each visit to the claim or invoice. They do not bill any visit that lacks matching documentation.
Billing staff never bill for services outside the authorization, for travel time unless the payer allows it, for time not worked, or for services not on the service plan.
Billing staff correct any mismatch before billing. Corrections are made by the person who made the error, with the date, reason and corrector's initials. Original entries are never deleted.

For Medicaid-funded services, the Agency Manager reviews EVV compliance each month and reports quarterly to the governing body against the HFS threshold of at least 75% quarterly EVV compliance from April 1, 2026. Visits that fall short are investigated and the cause is corrected.

If the agency finds an overbilling or underbilling error, the Agency Manager corrects it with the payer or client promptly, documents the amount, cause and correction, and reports it to the governing body.
The agency will not offer or accept anything of value to induce referrals of clients or in return for referrals.

Staff may report billing or compliance concerns to the Agency Manager, or to any member of the governing body if the concern involves the Agency Manager. Reports may be made orally or in writing, and anonymously through [CONFIDENTIAL REPORTING METHOD, e.g., a locked drop box or phone line].
The agency prohibits retaliation against anyone who reports a concern in good faith. Retaliation is grounds for discipline up to termination.

The Agency Manager logs each report, investigates within [NUMBER] business days, documents findings and actions, and reports substantiated fraud to the governing body and the affected payer or agency as required by that payer.
The agency keeps billing, EVV and investigation records for at least [NUMBER] years, or longer if a payer contract requires it.

responsibilities.duty: Oversees compliance; receives reports; acts on substantiated violations.
Trains staff; verifies rates and authorizations; monitors EVV compliance; investigates reports; reports to the governing body.
Match documentation and EVV to each claim; bill only authorized, delivered services; correct errors transparently.
Record accurate times and visit notes; report concerns.

documentation: Compliance training records and signed acknowledgments
Payer authorizations (CCP and HSP)
Rate verification log
Time sheet, visit note, EVV and claim reconciliations
EVV compliance reports
Compliance report log and investigation files
Governing body minutes recording compliance reports

policies.title: IDPH Surveys, Inspections and Complaint Investigations
policies.applies_to: Agency Manager, Alternate Agency Manager, office staff and supervisors
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] is ready for IDPH surveys and complaint investigations, cooperates fully, and corrects any deficiency promptly.
policies.policy:
IDPH conducts an on-site compliance survey within 30 days of the provisional license expiring. IDPH may also survey and investigate complaints at other times. [AGENCY NAME] cooperates fully with every IDPH visit and request. The agency names one person, the Agency Manager, with the Alternate Agency Manager as backup, to receive IDPH contacts and respond the same day.

IDPH surveyors check training records, annual Health Care Worker Registry verification and annual education, as described in IDPH's guidance for common deficiency findings. Training records must show the date, minutes per topic, instructor and qualifications, content and the worker's signature. The agency keeps these records survey-ready at all times.

The Agency Manager has read the Part 245 provisions on surveys, inspections and complaint investigations in full, and will update this policy so that it matches them exactly. Until then, the procedures below apply together with any instructions IDPH gives during a visit.

definitions.definition: An on-site IDPH review of the agency's operations, records and practices to determine compliance with the Act and Part 245.
An IDPH review of a complaint about the agency, which may include an on-site visit and interviews.
A finding by IDPH that the agency does not meet a requirement of the Act or Part 245.
The agency's written response describing how and when it will correct each deficiency.
The Agency Manager (or Alternate Agency Manager) who receives IDPH calls and visits.

procedures: The governing body names the Agency Manager as survey contact and the Alternate Agency Manager as backup. Both are listed with their direct phone numbers at the front desk and on the IDPH contact list at [PHONE].
The survey contact responds to any IDPH call, email or visit the same business day. Office staff are trained to take a message and notify the survey contact immediately.
The Agency Manager calendar-tracks the provisional license expiration date and expects the survey within 30 days after it (see GOV-02).

At least 60 days before provisional license expiration, and then at least annually, the Agency Manager conducts a mock survey. It checks policies, governing body minutes, personnel files, training records and client records.

The mock survey specifically checks, for every worker: background check and Registry check (PER-02); annual Registry verification and annual education (PER-05); training records showing date, minutes per topic, instructor and qualifications, content and worker signature (PER-06); competency evaluation (PER-04); and health evaluation and TB screening (PER-07).
The Agency Manager records any gaps found and corrects them before the survey. Corrections are documented without back-dating any record.

Records are kept organized and available at the agency office: policies, organizational chart, governing body minutes, personnel files, training records, client records, complaint log, incident log, QI records, insurance evidence and licenses.
When surveyors arrive, staff verify the surveyors' identification, notify the survey contact immediately and escort them to the Agency Manager.
The survey contact welcomes the surveyors, provides a workspace, and supplies requested records promptly. The contact keeps a log of every record provided and copy made.

Staff answer surveyors' questions truthfully and within their own knowledge. The Agency Manager may be present for staff interviews unless IDPH requests otherwise. No one may alter, hide or create records during a survey.
If surveyors ask to visit or contact clients, the Agency Manager arranges this in line with client rights and privacy (CR-01 and CR-03).
At the exit conference, the Agency Manager takes notes on all preliminary findings and asks for clarification of anything unclear. The Agency Manager briefs the governing body within 2 business days.

When IDPH issues a statement of deficiencies, the Agency Manager prepares a plan of correction and submits it within the deadline IDPH sets. The plan states for each deficiency the corrective action, the responsible person, the completion date and how the agency will prevent recurrence.

The Agency Manager verifies completion of each corrective action, documents evidence of correction, and reports to the governing body until all items are closed. Findings are also entered into the QI program (GOV-04).

For an IDPH complaint investigation, the Agency Manager notifies the governing body the same day, preserves all related records, and cooperates as with a survey. Staff are told that retaliation against a complainant or witness is prohibited.

The Agency Manager keeps all survey and investigation reports, plans of correction and correspondence for at least [NUMBER] years. The Agency Manager checks the Part 245 survey and complaint provisions annually and updates this policy accordingly (GOV-03).

responsibilities.duty: Names the survey contact; receives briefings; approves plans of correction; ensures resources for correction.
Responds to IDPH the same day; runs mock surveys; hosts surveys; prepares and completes plans of correction.
Acts as survey contact when the Agency Manager is unavailable.
Verify surveyor identity, notify the survey contact at once, and assist with records.
Cooperate truthfully; never alter records; never retaliate.

documentation: Survey contact designation and contact list
Mock survey checklists and results
Log of records provided to surveyors
IDPH survey reports and statements of deficiencies
Plans of correction with completion evidence
Complaint investigation files
Governing body minutes of survey briefings

policies.title: Notification of Changes to IDPH and New-County Approval
policies.applies_to: Governing body, Agency Manager and the named Licensing Compliance Designee
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] keeps its Illinois Home Services Agency license in good standing. The agency tells the Illinois Department of Public Health (IDPH) about changes on time, does not serve a new county before IDPH approves it, and renews the license before it expires.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] will notify IDPH within 10 days of any change to the agency, including a change of ownership, Agency Manager, address or telephone number. The notice will be made on the IDPH Facility Information Change Form. The agency will not accept or serve a client in any county not already approved on its license until IDPH has approved that county in writing. The agency will submit its renewal application before the full license expires. The agency will calendar a 90-day renewal reminder, because IDPH Form 445104 asks for renewal materials 60 days before expiration, and the 90-day reminder leaves time to gather them. The governing body names one person, the Licensing Compliance Designee ([LICENSING COMPLIANCE DESIGNEE NAME]), who owns every deadline in this policy. A named back-up covers that person's absences. The agency also tracks the provisional-license timeline: the provisional license is valid 240 days, it can be extended 120 days when substantial progress is shown, and IDPH holds a compliance survey within 30 days of the provisional license's expiration. The full license expires one year from the end of the month in which the provisional license was first issued.

definitions.definition: The IDPH form the agency uses to report changes in ownership, manager, address or telephone number.
The one named person responsible for IDPH notice, county-approval and renewal deadlines.
The initial license, valid 240 days and extendable 120 days if the agency shows substantial progress, issued before the full license.
Any county not already listed on the agency's current IDPH license or approvals.

procedures: 1. The governing body names the Licensing Compliance Designee and a back-up in writing, and records them on the organizational chart and in the governing body minutes.

2. On the day the provisional license is issued, the Designee enters the key dates on the shared compliance calendar: provisional expiration (240 days), the last date to request the 120-day extension, the expected IDPH compliance survey window (within 30 days of provisional expiration), and the full-license expiration date (one year from the end of the month the provisional license was first issued).

3. The Designee sets a 90-day pre-expiration renewal reminder for the full license, with a second reminder at 60 days that matches the Form 445104 renewal timing. Each reminder goes to the Designee, the back-up and the Agency Manager.

4. At the 90-day reminder, the Designee pulls the current IDPH renewal form and fee instructions. The Designee also confirms current liability insurance evidence (see GOV-09), the current policy manual (see GOV-03) and current manager information.
5. The Designee submits the renewal application and fee as IDPH instructs, no later than 60 days before expiration, and keeps a copy of everything sent along with proof of delivery.
6. Any employee who learns of a possible change in ownership, Agency Manager, address or telephone number tells the Agency Manager and the Designee the same business day.

7. The Designee completes the Facility Information Change Form within 5 business days of learning of the change. This internal target leaves margin under the 10-day IDPH limit. The Designee sends it to IDPH at DPH.COOS@illinois.gov or by the method IDPH requires.
8. The Designee records the date of the change, the date IDPH was notified, how it was sent and any IDPH acknowledgment on the Change Notification Log.

9. For a change of ownership, the Designee also confirms with IDPH whether a new application is required and completes it before the change takes effect. The governing body will not treat a notice form as a substitute for a required application.

10. When the agency plans to add a county, the Agency Manager brings a written expansion plan to the governing body. It covers caregiver availability, supervisory visit capacity (see SVC-04 and SVC-05) and office or after-hours coverage (see GOV-08).
11. After governing body approval, the Designee submits the new-county request to IDPH and keeps the submission proof in the licensing file.

12. The Designee tells the intake staff in writing that the county is not approved. Intake staff do not accept, schedule or begin services for a client in that county until the Designee issues written notice of IDPH's written approval.

13. When IDPH approves the county, the Designee files the approval, updates the county list in the licensing file, intake screening tools and advertising (see GOV-02), and tells the Agency Manager and scheduling staff.
14. If a client in an unapproved county contacts the agency, intake staff refer the person to another licensed agency and record the referral. They do not provide any service.
15. When IDPH schedules a survey, the Designee notifies the Agency Manager immediately (see GOV-06).

16. The Designee reports to the governing body at each meeting on upcoming deadlines, pending IDPH submissions and any missed or late items. The governing body corrects any gap and records the correction.

policies.title: Office, Operating Hours and After-Hours Access
policies.applies_to: Agency Manager, office staff, on-call staff and all caregivers
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] maintains a compliant office and tells every client in writing when the office is open and how to reach the agency when it is closed.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] maintains an office at [ADDRESS] with a working telephone, [PHONE], that is staffed during business hours (77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.40(a)). The office protects the confidentiality of client and personnel records, and it complies with applicable fire-safety ordinances. The agency's written operating hours are [DAYS AND HOURS OF OPERATION]. Outside those hours, clients, representatives and caregivers can reach a trained on-call staff member at [AFTER-HOURS PHONE]. Operating hours and after-hours access instructions are given to every client in writing before services begin. In an emergency, clients are told to call 911 first and the agency second.

definitions.definition: The days and hours stated in the agency's written operating-hours policy, during which the office telephone is answered by staff.
The method, including telephone number and on-call staff, by which clients and caregivers reach the agency when the office is closed.
A trained agency employee designated on a posted schedule to answer after-hours calls and take action.

procedures: 1. The Agency Manager keeps the office open and the telephone staffed during the hours stated in this policy. If the staffed telephone cannot be covered for any reason, the Agency Manager or the designee for the manager's absence arranges coverage the same day.
2. The Agency Manager posts the operating hours at the office entrance and prints them in the client agreement packet and in the client handbook.

3. Intake staff give every client or representative a written copy of the operating hours and the after-hours number before the first visit, review it verbally, and note the review in the client record.
4. The Agency Manager publishes a monthly on-call schedule. Each on-call staff member must have a charged phone, access to the client schedule and contact list, and this policy.
5. The after-hours telephone message states the operating hours, tells callers to dial 911 for any emergency, and gives the after-hours number or instructions for reaching the on-call staff member.

6. The on-call staff member returns every after-hours message within 30 minutes. For a missed visit, caregiver absence or client emergency, the on-call staff member acts as set out in SVC-09 and SVC-11.

7. The on-call staff member writes up each after-hours contact on the After-Hours Contact Log (caller, time, issue, action taken, follow-up needed). The log is reviewed by the Agency Manager on the next business day.

8. The Agency Manager keeps client records in locked cabinets or access-controlled electronic systems. Records are not left on desks or in view of visitors. Visitors do not go unescorted into record areas.

9. The Agency Manager conducts and documents a fire-safety walk-through at least annually. The walk-through checks exits, extinguishers, smoke detectors and any local ordinance requirements. Findings are corrected promptly.

10. The Agency Manager confirms with the local fire authority or building department, and records, which fire-safety ordinances apply to the office. The agency keeps any inspection or certificate on file.

11. If the office address or telephone number changes, the Agency Manager updates the operating-hours notices and gives clients written notice within 5 business days. The Licensing Compliance Designee sends the IDPH notice as required by GOV-07.
12. The Agency Manager reviews call and message logs quarterly for unanswered calls and slow call-backs. Findings go to the quality improvement program (see GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Keeps the office staffed and compliant, publishes hours and the on-call schedule, and reviews logs.
Answer the office telephone in business hours, protect records and give clients the written hours.

Know the after-hours number and use it to report absences, incidents or emergencies.
