A worker who feels unsafe at any time may leave the home and call the supervisor at [PHONE]. If there is immediate danger, the worker first goes to a safe place and calls 911. The worker does not need approval to leave.
Workers do not handle, move or hold firearms or other weapons. If a weapon is visible or the client displays one, the worker leaves and reports it.

The Supervisor responds to any safety call right away, speaks to the worker, and decides whether to send a second person, change the visit time, or hold the visit. The worker is paid for the scheduled shift if they leave because of a danger beyond their control, as set out in PER-09.

The worker completes an Incident Report Form for any threat, assault, injury or hazard encounter within 24 hours (SAF-03). Workers who are injured are referred for medical care and the workers' compensation process (GOV-09).

The Agency Manager reviews every report within one business day. If a hazard or behavior can be reduced, the Agency Manager meets with the client or representative, adds controls to the service plan, and sets a date to recheck.

If a hazard cannot be controlled or a client threatens or assaults a worker, the Agency Manager may suspend visits, require two workers, or discontinue services under SVC-12. The Agency Manager notifies the payer program and the care coordinator (SVC-13). Police are notified when a crime has occurred.

Workers who are threatened or assaulted are offered a debrief with the Agency Manager, time off if needed, and a different assignment if they ask. The agency prohibits retaliation against any worker who reports a safety concern.

Workers who work alone or at night follow the check-in procedure in the Worker Safety Guide. The after-hours supervisor [PHONE] is available at all times visits are scheduled (GOV-08). Workers keep their personal information confidential from clients.
Workplace violence or harassment by a co-worker or supervisor is reported to the Agency Manager, or to the Governing Body if the Agency Manager is involved. It is investigated promptly under PER-13.
The Agency Manager reviews all safety reports at least quarterly and brings trends and corrective actions to Quality Improvement (GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Complete the home safety and worker risk checklist at intake and record hazards and controls.
Recheck hazards at supervisory visits, brief workers, respond to safety calls and support the worker.
Follow safety precautions, report hazards and incidents, and use stop-work authority when needed.
Resolve safety concerns with clients, decide on suspending or discharging, review reports, and ensure no retaliation.

documentation: Home Safety and Worker Risk Checklist at intake and each supervisory visit
Service plan entries for hazard controls
Worker briefing record
Incident Report Forms for threats, assaults and hazards
Training records on safety precautions
Quality Improvement minutes showing safety review

policies.title: Transporting Clients
policies.applies_to: All employees and contracted caregivers who transport clients, and their supervisors, at [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To make sure that transport to appointments, a service the agency may offer, is provided safely, with qualified drivers, adequate insurance, and the client's written consent.
policies.policy: Transport to appointments is a permitted service for a home services agency under 77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.210(a). [AGENCY NAME] provides it only to clients whose service plan includes transport and who have signed a transport consent. Only workers who have a valid driver's license, current auto insurance and an acceptable driving record may transport clients. The agency confirms that its liability insurance, including hired and non-owned auto coverage, covers this activity. The agency must show evidence of liability insurance (77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.90(a)). Transport is limited to getting the client to and from the destination safely. Workers follow the task limits for assisting with transfers (SVC-07) and do not lift a client who cannot bear weight.

definitions.definition: Liability insurance that covers the agency when employees drive their own or rented vehicles on agency business.
Moving a client between bed, chair, wheelchair, toilet or vehicle.

procedures: The Agency Manager confirms with the insurance carrier or broker, in writing and at each renewal, that the agency's liability policy includes hired and non-owned auto coverage and covers client transport. The confirmation is kept in the insurance file (GOV-09).

Before a worker is approved to drive clients, the Supervisor collects a copy of a valid driver's license and proof of current personal auto insurance, and checks the Illinois driving record. These are filed in the personnel record (PER-11).

The Agency Manager does not approve a worker who has a suspended or revoked license, an expired insurance policy, or a record of serious or repeated moving violations. The agency repeats the check at least annually.

The assessor decides at intake whether transport is requested, which destinations are covered, and whether the client can safely ride in a regular passenger vehicle. The decision is written in the service plan (SVC-02, SVC-03).

The client or representative signs the Transportation Consent and Risk Acknowledgment before the first trip. It states who owns the vehicle used, mileage or fees as set out in the service agreement (CR-06), and what assistance the worker will and will not give.

Clients who use a wheelchair, oxygen, or need more than standby help are transported only if the vehicle can safely carry them and the worker is trained. Otherwise the supervisor arranges for a medical transport provider.
Before each trip, the worker checks that the vehicle is clean, the seatbelts work and the client's mobility aids will fit. The worker confirms the destination, time and return plan with the client.
Everyone in the vehicle wears a seatbelt. The worker does not use a handheld phone, smoke, or drive when impaired, drowsy or ill. The worker never leaves a client alone in a vehicle.

The worker follows the transfer limits in SVC-07. The worker provides standby or steadying help only and does not lift a client who cannot bear weight. If a safe transfer is not possible, the worker does not attempt it and calls the supervisor.

The worker accompanies the client to the door of the appointment, or into the appointment if the service plan says so, and brings the client home. The worker does not give medical consent for the client or discuss the client's care with the provider unless the client has authorized it (CR-03).

The worker records each trip in the visit documentation: date, start and end time, mileage, destination, and any problems (REC-04). The worker keeps receipts for any client money handled and follows CR-04.

If there is a collision, injury, breakdown or other event during transport, the worker calls 911 if anyone is hurt, then the supervisor. The worker completes an Incident Report Form within 24 hours (SAF-03). The Agency Manager notifies the insurer.
Mileage reimbursement for worker-owned vehicles is paid according to PER-09 and PER-15. Travel time during a shift is counted as work time.
The Agency Manager reviews transport incidents and driver records at Quality Improvement each quarter (GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Hold a valid license and insurance, drive safely, follow transfer limits, document each trip and report incidents.
Verify license, insurance and driving record, obtain client consent, and monitor transport during supervisory visits.
Confirm insurance coverage, approve drivers, notify the insurer of incidents and review transport safety.

documentation: Insurance confirmation of hired and non-owned auto coverage
Copy of driver's license, proof of auto insurance and driving record in the personnel record
Signed Transportation Consent and Risk Acknowledgment in the client record
Service plan showing transport as an authorized service
Trip records with mileage
Incident Report Forms for transport events

policies.title: Caregiver Qualifications, Registry and Employment Conditions
policies.applies_to: All applicants for, and employees in, caregiver and other positions at [AGENCY NAME], including licensed, certified or registered staff
policies.purpose: To set the qualifications and the documents every caregiver must have before working for [AGENCY NAME], including background check, Health Care Worker Registry, work authorization, and license verification.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] employs only workers who meet the conditions in this policy. For each worker who is not otherwise licensed, certified or registered, the employee file contains documentation of (1) no disqualifying Health Care Worker Background Check, or a waiver where one has been granted, (2) a copy of the Social Security card, and (3) a visa or proof of citizenship that meets federal employment requirements (77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.71(a)). The agency complies with the Health Care Worker Background Check Act (225 ILCS 46) and the Health Care Worker Background Check Code (77 Ill. Adm. Code 955), as required by 77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.72. Before employing anyone in a position that needs a State professional license, the agency verifies with the Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation (IDFPR) that the license is active and keeps a copy in the personnel file (245.30(c)(2)). A worker who is a Certified Nursing Assistant on the Health Care Worker Registry may have prior training accepted toward initial training, but must still pass the competency evaluation before first assignment (PER-04).

definitions.definition: A fingerprint-based criminal history check required by 225 ILCS 46 for covered workers. When it is initiated through IDPH, the results are entered in the IDPH Health Care Worker Registry.
A conviction for an offense that bars employment in a covered position under 225 ILCS 46 and 77 Ill. Adm. Code 955, unless a waiver has been granted.
A written decision under the Health Care Worker Background Check Act that allows a person with a disqualifying conviction to be employed.
The IDPH registry of health care workers, which includes background check results and findings of abuse, neglect or misappropriation.
A position, such as nurse, that requires a State professional license issued by IDFPR.

procedures: The Agency Manager confirms before the first hire that [AGENCY NAME] has access to the IDPH Health Care Worker Registry. Proof of access is kept with the license application documents (955.115, per IDPH Form 445104) and is renewed as needed.

Each applicant completes the employment application and provides government photo identification. The application lists work history and references. The Agency Manager checks at least two references and records the results.

The Agency Manager checks that the applicant meets the position's job description (PER-10). Minimum caregiver requirements are the ability to read, write and follow instructions in English or the language of the clients served, physical ability to do the work, and willingness to complete required training.

Before any client contact, the Agency Manager completes the federal Form I-9 with the applicant and keeps a copy of the visa or proof of citizenship that meets federal employment requirements. A copy of the Social Security card is kept in the employee file.

The Agency Manager starts the Health Care Worker Background Check (PER-02). Fingerprints are taken and submitted so that they are sent to the Illinois State Police within the 10-working-day timeframe set by the Act and Code.

The Agency Manager checks the IDPH Health Care Worker Registry for each applicant and records the date and result. A finding of abuse, neglect or misappropriation of property on the Registry bars employment.

The Agency Manager does not schedule the worker for unsupervised client contact until fingerprint results have been received and show no disqualifying offense, or a waiver has been granted. A waiver is kept in the personnel file.

If the results show a disqualifying conviction, the Agency Manager does not hire the person unless a waiver is granted. The Agency Manager follows the Code's procedure for notifying the applicant and applying for a waiver, and documents each step.

For any position that needs a State professional license, the Agency Manager looks up the license on the IDFPR website before hire. The Agency Manager prints or saves a copy showing it is active and files it in the personnel file (245.30(c)(2)). The agency repeats the check at each renewal date.

For workers who are Certified Nursing Assistants on the Health Care Worker Registry, the Agency Manager may accept their prior training toward the initial training topics after reviewing the certificate, but the worker must still complete orientation and pass the competency evaluation before first assignment (PER-03, PER-04).

Before first assignment, the applicant also completes the health evaluation and tuberculosis screening (PER-07). The worker signs the confidentiality statement, the abuse and neglect reporting acknowledgment and the code of conduct (PER-13).

The Agency Manager completes the New Hire Qualification Checklist and verifies that the file contains: name and address, Social Security number and card copy, date of birth, next of kin, evidence of qualifications, background check and Registry results, proof of work authorization, employment date, and, if applicable, the license verification (PER-11, C7). The Agency Manager signs and dates the checklist before the worker's first assignment.
Each year, the Agency Manager rechecks the Health Care Worker Registry for every worker (PER-05) and removes from client contact anyone who has a new disqualifying finding.
The worker must notify the Agency Manager within 3 business days of any arrest, conviction, license discipline or Registry finding. Failure to do so is grounds for discipline up to discharge.
When a worker leaves, the Agency Manager records the date and reason for separation in the personnel file (PER-11).

responsibilities.duty: Verify every qualification, run background check and Registry checks, verify licenses with IDFPR, and sign the New Hire Qualification Checklist before first assignment.
Do not schedule any worker for client contact who has not been cleared by the Agency Manager.
Provide accurate documents, complete fingerprinting and report any changes in criminal, license or Registry status.
Ensure the agency has Registry access and the resources to carry out this policy.

documentation: Employment application and reference checks
Copy of Social Security card
Visa or proof of citizenship and Form I-9
Health Care Worker Background Check results and any waiver
Health Care Worker Registry check with date and result
IDFPR license verification copy for licensed positions
Proof of agency access to the IDPH Health Care Worker Registry
New Hire Qualification Checklist signed by the Agency Manager

policies.title: Background Checks and Health Care Worker Registry
policies.applies_to: All applicants, employees and contracted or placed workers who may have direct client contact or access to client homes, records or property; Agency Manager; Home Services Supervisors; personnel coordinator
policies.purpose: To make sure every person who provides in-home services for [AGENCY NAME] has had the fingerprint-based Health Care Worker Background Check required by Illinois law, is checked on the IDPH Health Care Worker Registry, and has that status re-verified every year.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] complies with the Health Care Worker Background Check Act (225 ILCS 46) and the Health Care Worker Background Check Code (77 Ill. Adm. Code 955), as required by 77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.72. No person is assigned to a client until the agency has completed the background check process and the worker's file shows no disqualifying result, or a valid waiver. Fingerprints are sent to the Illinois State Police within 10 working days, and results initiated through IDPH are entered in the Health Care Worker Registry. The agency keeps proof of access to the IDPH Health Care Worker Registry. The agency verifies each worker on the Registry every year. This policy is the agency's written background check process and meets IDPH Form 445104, p. 8 (955.145, 955.165, 955.220) (initial applicants only: health care worker background check process). The agency follows the process requirements of 77 Ill. Adm. Code 955, including 955.145, 955.165 and 955.220, as they are currently published. The Agency Manager reviews those sections whenever this policy is reviewed.

definitions.definition: The fingerprint-based criminal history check required by 225 ILCS 46 and 77 Ill. Adm. Code 955 for covered workers.
The IDPH registry in which results of background checks initiated through IDPH are entered and which the agency checks to verify worker status.
A conviction that bars employment in a covered position under the Act unless a waiver has been granted.
Written permission granted under the Act and Code allowing employment despite a disqualifying conviction.
Any employee, contracted or placed worker who has direct care or access to clients, their living quarters, or their financial, medical or personal records.

procedures: Before the agency opens its first client case, the Agency Manager confirms that the agency has access to the IDPH Health Care Worker Registry and files proof of that access (955.115) in the licensing file.
Every job application and offer letter states that employment is conditional on a satisfactory Health Care Worker Background Check and on Registry verification.
The personnel coordinator identifies each applicant as a covered worker before the first day of work. All home services workers are covered.
For a worker who is otherwise licensed, certified or registered (for example a CNA), the personnel coordinator still checks the Registry before assignment and files the result.
The applicant is told in writing what the check involves, and completes and signs the consent and authorization forms required by the Act and Code.
The applicant is directed to a fingerprint vendor approved for the Illinois process. The personnel coordinator records the date the fingerprint request was initiated.

The personnel coordinator submits or confirms submission of the fingerprints and required information to the Illinois State Police within 10 working days of the applicant's authorization, and notes the date in the personnel file.

The agency follows the procedural steps for initiating, tracking and recording checks set out in 77 Ill. Adm. Code 955, including 955.145, 955.165 and 955.220, and tracks every pending check on a background check log.

The personnel coordinator reviews the results and checks the Registry for the worker. The worker is not scheduled for any client visit until the result shows no disqualifying conviction, or a waiver is on file.

If the result shows a disqualifying conviction, the Agency Manager does not assign the worker. The Agency Manager decides, with the governing body, whether to pursue a waiver under the Act and Code. No assignment is made until the waiver is granted.

The personnel coordinator files in the employee file the documentation required by 245.71(a): the background check result showing no disqualifying finding or the waiver, a copy of the Social Security card, and a visa or proof of citizenship that meets federal employment requirements.

Each year, within 30 days before the worker's training year ends (see PER-05), the personnel coordinator checks every active worker on the Registry, prints or saves the result with the date and verifier's initials, and files it in the personnel file.
If an annual check shows a new disqualifying finding, or a worker reports an arrest or conviction, the Agency Manager removes the worker from client contact the same day and follows the Act and Code.
A worker must tell the Agency Manager within 24 hours of any new criminal charge or conviction. Failure to do so is grounds for discipline.

The Agency Manager reviews the background check log quarterly to make sure no check is overdue, no unverified worker is on the schedule, and every annual verification has been done. Results go to the quality improvement program (GOV-04).
Background check records are kept confidential under PER-11 and are available to IDPH surveyors on request.

responsibilities.duty: Adopts this policy and decides on waiver requests with the Agency Manager.
Confirms Registry access, ensures no unchecked worker is scheduled, removes workers with disqualifying findings, and reviews the log quarterly.
Starts fingerprinting, tracks submission dates, checks the Registry, and files results and employment documents.
Assigns only workers shown as cleared on the background check log.
Completes the check, supplies identity and work-authorization documents, and reports new charges or convictions within 24 hours.

Signed applicant consent and authorization forms
Background check log with fingerprint initiation and submission dates
Background check result and Registry printout or screenshot for each worker, with date and verifier initials
Waiver documents, if any
Copy of Social Security card and visa or proof of citizenship (I-9 documents) in each employee file
Annual Registry verification record for each worker

policies.title: Orientation and Initial Training (10 Hours)
policies.applies_to: All newly hired home services workers; Home Services Supervisors and trainers; personnel coordinator
policies.purpose: To make sure every home services worker is oriented to the agency and completes the initial training required by Illinois rule before serving clients.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] provides or arranges at least 10 hours of initial training for every home services worker. At least 5 hours are completed before the worker's first assignment, and the remaining 5 hours within 30 days of the start of employment (77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.71(c)). No worker is given an assignment until the worker passes a competency evaluation on the topics of the first 5 hours (see PER-04). This policy meets IDPH Form 445104, p. 8 (245.71) (initial applicants only: employee training procedures), and 77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.30(c)(1)(C) (personnel policies: orientation to the agency and appropriate continuing education). Continuing education is addressed in PER-05. The agency does not use the 8-hour figure, which applies only to placement agencies. The agency may accept proof of training from another licensed home services agency within the prior 365 days, including a CNA on the Health Care Worker Registry, but the worker still receives a competency evaluation before the first assignment.

definitions.definition: The minimum 10 hours of training required for each new home services worker under 245.71(c).
Instruction on the agency's organization, policies, client rights, the worker's job description and reporting lines, included in the first 5 hours.
Training documented by another licensed home services agency within the previous 365 days.
A test by a qualified supervisor or trainer, through demonstration or written or oral means, that the worker can perform the tasks and apply the topics taught.

procedures: The personnel coordinator opens a training record for each new worker on or before the start date, showing the start date, the date by which hour 5 must be done (before the first assignment) and the date by which hour 10 must be done (30 days after the start of employment).

At hire, the personnel coordinator asks the worker for proof of any training by another licensed home services agency within the prior 365 days, including CNA status on the Health Care Worker Registry. The trainer reviews the proof and decides in writing what hours and topics, if any, can be credited. Credited topics are still reviewed with the worker.

The Home Services Supervisor or trainer gives orientation to the agency during the first 5 hours. This covers the agency's organization and chain of command, the worker's job description (PER-10), personnel policies (PER-09), client rights (CR-01), confidentiality (CR-03), and nondiscrimination under the Civil Rights Act of 1964 (CR-05).

The first 5 hours are completed before the first assignment and cover the topics of 245.71(e) that are needed to work safely from day one: job responsibilities and limits; communication with people who are hard of hearing or have dementia; observing, reporting and documenting; personal care tasks including medication reminding; hygiene and infection control; a clean and safe environment; safety precautions; emergencies, first aid and the client's emergency preparedness plan; confidentiality; and abuse and neglect and reporting duties.
The first 5 hours also include the ADL tasks in 245.40(c)(4)(A)-(P) that the worker will be assigned, as well as adaptive equipment and any other task the agency assigns.

Training on understanding dementia and problem-solving for challenging dementia behaviors is completed in the initial training using the content in SVC-08, and in any case before the worker is assigned to a client with dementia.

The trainer gives the competency evaluation on the first 5 hours' topics (PER-04). A worker who does not pass receives more instruction and is re-evaluated. The worker is not assigned until the evaluation is passed.

The remaining 5 hours are completed within 30 days of the start of employment. The trainer finishes any topics from 245.71(e)(1)-(14) not yet covered, and gives the second competency evaluation after these hours.
A worker who has not completed the second 5 hours by day 30 is taken off the schedule until training is finished, and the Agency Manager is notified.
Each training session is documented under PER-06: date, minutes per topic, instructor and qualifications, content description, and worker signature or electronic certificate with date and time stamp.
The trainer reviews this content at least yearly and updates it when rules, client needs or agency policies change.
The Agency Manager reviews the training log monthly and reports late training to the governing body and the quality improvement program (GOV-04).
Completion of the initial 10 hours counts as the worker's required training for the first year of employment (see PER-05).

responsibilities.duty: Ensures resources for training, enforces the 'no assignment before training and evaluation' rule and reviews the training log monthly.
Delivers or arranges orientation and training, evaluates credit for prior training, gives competency evaluations and documents training.
Sets up training records and due dates, and files proof of prior training.
Attends and completes all training, passes the evaluations, and signs training records.

documentation: Individual training record showing hours and due dates
Training roster per session with date, minutes per topic, instructor and qualifications, content description and worker signature or electronic certificate with date/time stamp
Proof of prior training from another licensed home services agency and the trainer's credit decision
Competency evaluation results for the first 5 hours and the second 5 hours
Signed acknowledgement of orientation and job description
Monthly training log review

policies.title: Competency Evaluation Before First Assignment
policies.applies_to: All home services workers; Home Services Supervisors and trainers
policies.purpose: To make sure no worker is sent to a client's home until the worker has shown that he or she can do the job safely and within the limits set by Illinois rule.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] does not give any assignment to a home services worker until the worker passes a competency evaluation on the topics of the first 5 hours of initial training. A second competency evaluation follows the remaining 5 hours. Workers who bring proof of training from another licensed home services agency within the prior 365 days (including a CNA on the Health Care Worker Registry) still receive a competency evaluation before the first assignment. Task-specific competency evaluations are required for the personal care tasks under 77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.40(c)(4) before the worker performs those tasks. This policy meets IDPH Form 445104, p. 8 (245.71) (initial applicants only: employee training procedures). Results are kept in the personnel file.

definitions.definition: A documented assessment by a qualified supervisor or trainer that the worker understands the training topics and can correctly perform the tasks.
An evaluation of a worker's ability to perform a specific task listed in 245.40(c)(4), such as bathing, ambulation or positioning, in the method taught.
A Home Services Supervisor or trainer who meets the qualifications in PER-06.

procedures: The trainer completes the first 5 hours of training (PER-03) and then schedules the competency evaluation for the same day or as soon after as possible. The worker is not scheduled for any client visit until it is passed.

The evaluation covers the first 5 hours' topics: job responsibilities and limits; communication with people who are hard of hearing or have dementia; observing, reporting and documenting; hygiene and infection control; a safe environment; emergencies and first aid; confidentiality; and abuse and neglect reporting.

The evaluation uses the agency's standard form, with written or oral questions plus direct demonstration of hands-on skills. Each worker is judged against the same pass criteria set by the Agency Manager.
The qualified evaluator marks each item as competent or not yet competent, signs and dates the form, and the worker signs it.

If the worker does not pass, the evaluator documents the gaps, retrains the worker on those items and re-evaluates. A worker who cannot pass after retraining is not assigned, and the Agency Manager decides on next steps.
A worker with proof of prior training from another licensed agency, or a CNA on the Registry, takes the same competency evaluation before the first assignment. Prior training does not replace it.

Before the worker performs any task covered by 245.40(c)(4)(A)-(P) (for example skin care, ambulation, bathing, dressing/compression, exercise, feeding/thickener, hair care, mouth care, nail care, positioning, shaving, toileting), the evaluator confirms the worker has been trained in the method and passes a task-specific competency evaluation on that task.

For tasks that require client or client-representative feedback, or a health care professional's order, the Home Services Supervisor confirms and records these in the service plan (SVC-03) before assigning the task. The competency evaluation does not replace them.
The evaluator does not approve evaluation of passive range of motion, nail trimming or skilled skin care. These are outside the home services scope (SVC-01).
After the remaining 5 hours of training are completed (within 30 days of the start of employment), the evaluator gives the second competency evaluation on those topics and documents the result.

Workers are re-evaluated on a task when the client's condition or method changes, when observation shows incorrect technique (SVC-05), or when the worker has been away from a task for an extended period.
The evaluator files all evaluation records in the personnel file within 2 business days. The scheduler is told in writing that the worker is cleared for assignment.
The Agency Manager audits new-hire files quarterly to check that each worker has a passed evaluation dated before the first assignment, and reports the findings to the quality improvement program.

responsibilities.duty: Sets pass criteria and approves evaluation forms, and audits that no worker was assigned before passing.
Conducts and documents the evaluations, retrains and re-evaluates, and clears workers for assignment.
Assigns work only to workers with written clearance.
Participates in the evaluations and performs only the tasks he or she has been cleared to do.

documentation: Competency evaluation form for the first 5 hours, signed by evaluator and worker, with date
Competency evaluation form for the second 5 hours
Task-specific competency records for each 245.40(c)(4) task
Retraining and re-evaluation records
Written clearance for assignment
Quarterly new-hire audit

policies.title: Annual Training and Annual Registry Verification
policies.applies_to: All home services workers; Home Services Supervisors and trainers; personnel coordinator
policies.purpose: To make sure every worker receives at least 10 hours of training each year on the required topics and that every worker's Health Care Worker Registry status is verified each year.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] provides each home services worker at least 10 hours of training per year of employment, as required by 77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.71(f). The agency uses a [calendar-year / anniversary-date] training year, chosen by the governing body and applied to all workers. The worker's initial 10 hours satisfy the first year of employment. Self-study is allowed when the worker demonstrates what was learned. The agency also verifies every worker on the Health Care Worker Registry each year, which is a focus of IDPH surveys. This policy meets IDPH Form 445104, p. 8 (245.71) (initial applicants only: employee training procedures).

definitions.definition: The 12-month period used to count annual training, either the calendar year or each worker's employment anniversary, as chosen by the agency.
Independent learning such as readings or recorded courses, accepted only when the worker shows learning through a test, written summary or demonstration.
A yearly check of the Health Care Worker Registry for each worker, with the result filed in the personnel file.

procedures: The governing body adopts one training-year method (calendar-year or anniversary) and the Agency Manager records it in the training plan.

By December 1 each year (or 60 days before each worker's anniversary), the personnel coordinator prints a list of each worker's hours completed in the current training year and the hours still needed.
The trainer builds an annual training calendar so each worker can complete at least 10 hours per year. Sessions are offered in person, online or as self-study, and at times that fit worker schedules.

Each year's training includes: client dignity, independence, self-determination, privacy, choice and rights; disaster procedures; hygiene and infection control; abuse and neglect prevention and reporting; and the ADL tasks in 245.40(c)(4)(A)-(P). Training on oxygen delivery is included for workers who serve clients on oxygen (SVC-07).

The trainer also includes dementia refreshers (SVC-08), changes in policy, and topics from the quality improvement program, incident trends or supervisory visit findings, as time within the 10 hours permits.

For self-study, the trainer assigns the material, sets the minutes credited, and requires a quiz, written summary or demonstration. The worker receives credit only after demonstrated learning is documented.
Each session is documented under PER-06: date, minutes per topic, instructor and qualifications, content description and worker signature or electronic certificate with date and time stamp.
Hours are counted by the minutes documented per topic. Only completed, documented time is credited.

The Home Services Supervisor notifies workers who are behind at 90 days and 30 days before the end of their training year. A worker who has not completed 10 hours by the end of the training year is not scheduled for new assignments until the hours are complete, and the Agency Manager is notified.

Within 30 days before the end of each worker's training year, the personnel coordinator checks the worker on the Health Care Worker Registry, saves a dated printout or screenshot with verifier initials in the personnel file, and enters the date on the verification log.
If the Registry shows a disqualifying finding or other problem, the Agency Manager removes the worker from client contact immediately and follows PER-02.
The Agency Manager reviews the annual training and Registry verification report at each quality improvement meeting (GOV-04) and keeps it available for IDPH surveyors.

responsibilities.duty: Chooses calendar-year or anniversary basis and supports adequate training time.
Ensures all workers complete training and Registry verification, and reviews the compliance report.
Plans and delivers annual training, verifies self-study learning and tracks hours.
Tracks hours and due dates, performs and files the annual Registry verification.
Completes at least 10 hours of training each year and signs all training records.

documentation: Annual training plan and calendar
Individual training record showing hours and minutes by topic for each training year
Session rosters with instructor, qualifications, content, and worker signature or electronic certificate with date/time stamp
Self-study assignments and proof of demonstrated learning
Annual Health Care Worker Registry verification printout and log
Reminder notices and any scheduling restrictions for overdue workers

policies.title: Training Documentation and Trainer/Supervisor Qualifications
policies.applies_to: Agency Manager; Home Services Supervisors and trainers; personnel coordinator; all home services workers
policies.purpose: To make sure all training is fully documented in the way Illinois rule requires and that only qualified people supervise and train home services workers.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] has home services supervisors or trainers who give initial training and ongoing supervision. Each supervisor and trainer meets one of the qualifications in 77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.71(g)-(h): (1) at least 2 years of qualifying experience within the last 5 years, or (2) a current supervisory or trainer position and training within the past year on the permitted tasks, provided by or developed by a qualified professional. Supervisors and trainers are available to workers for continuing education. All training is documented under 245.71(i) with the date, minutes per topic, instructor and qualifications, content description, and worker signature or electronic certificate with date and time stamp. This policy meets IDPH Form 445104, p. 8 (245.71) (initial applicants only: employee training procedures).

definitions.definition: Work experience relevant to the in-home services and tasks the person will supervise or teach, documented in writing with employers and dates.
A licensed health care professional, such as a registered nurse or therapist, who provides or develops training on the permitted tasks.
A computer-generated completion record that shows the worker's name, course, and date and time stamp, accepted in place of a handwritten signature.

procedures: Before assigning any person as a supervisor or trainer, the Agency Manager verifies in writing that the person meets option (1) or option (2) of the qualification standard.

For option (1), the personnel coordinator obtains a resume or employment verification showing at least 2 years of qualifying experience within the last 5 years, and files it in the person's personnel file.

For option (2), the personnel coordinator files proof that the person currently holds a supervisory or trainer position and a record of training on the permitted tasks within the past year, including the name and credentials of the qualified professional who provided or developed it.

Every year, the Agency Manager re-checks each supervisor's and trainer's qualification. Option (2) people complete refresher training on the permitted tasks within each 12-month period, and it is documented.

The Agency Manager publishes to all workers the names and contact information of supervisors and trainers and the hours they are available ([PHONE]). Workers can ask for continuing education or help at any time, and requests are answered within 3 business days.

Each training session uses the agency's training roster or electronic system, which collects the date, minutes spent on each topic, instructor name and qualifications, a description of the content, and each worker's signature or electronic certificate with date and time stamp.

The instructor completes and signs the roster on the day of training. For online or self-study courses, the system certificate and the evidence of demonstrated learning are filed in the worker's record.
The personnel coordinator enters the training into each worker's training record within 5 business days and files rosters in the personnel file.
Where an outside vendor or professional provides training, the agency obtains the instructor's name and qualifications, a content outline and attendance records, and keeps them with the roster.

The personnel coordinator performs a monthly check that rosters are complete (all required fields filled in) and corrects any gap while the training is still recent. Incomplete records are not counted toward required hours until they are corrected.
Training records are kept in the personnel file for the length of employment and as long as required under PER-11, and are made available to IDPH surveyors on request.
The Agency Manager reports the results of the monthly check, and any trainer or supervisor qualification gaps, to the quality improvement program (GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Verifies and re-verifies qualifications of supervisors and trainers and ensures records are complete.
Meets the qualification standard, is available to workers, and completes accurate rosters.
Files qualification proof, enters training data and audits rosters monthly.
Signs or electronically certifies each training session and requests continuing education when needed.

documentation: Supervisor and trainer qualification proof (experience verification or position plus current-year training record)
Annual qualification re-verification
Training roster or electronic certificate showing date, minutes per topic, instructor and qualifications, content description and worker signature or date/time stamp
Outside vendor instructor credentials and content outlines
Supervisor and trainer availability notice
Monthly roster audit

policies.title: Initial Employee Health Evaluation and TB Screening
policies.applies_to: All new employees and placed or contracted workers who have contact with clients; Agency Manager; personnel coordinator
policies.purpose: To protect clients and workers by making sure each new worker with client contact has an initial health evaluation, including TB screening, as specified by the governing body before working with clients.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] requires an initial health evaluation of each new employee, or placed or contracted worker, who has contact with clients, as specified by the governing body (77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.30(c)(1)(B)). The rule does not name a specific TB test, so the governing body sets the requirement in writing in this policy. This policy meets 77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.30(c)(1)(B) (personnel policies: requirements for an initial health evaluation of each new employee, or placed worker, who has contact with clients, as specified by the governing body). The governing body requires: (1) an evaluation by a licensed health care professional (physician, advanced practice registered nurse, physician assistant or registered nurse) or an occupational health clinic, that confirms the person can perform the essential job functions with or without reasonable accommodation and is free of signs of communicable disease; and (2) TB screening consisting of a symptom screen and a TB test (tuberculin skin test or blood test) with results documented, completed before the first client contact. Results are confidential and are kept apart from the personnel file.

definitions.definition: A health review of a new worker by a licensed health care professional, confirming the worker is free of communicable disease and able to do the job, performed before client contact.
A symptom screen and a TB test (tuberculin skin test or blood test) with the result documented.
Any in-person contact with a client or visit to a client's home as part of the worker's job.
A change in how a job is done that lets a qualified person with a disability or condition do the essential functions.

procedures: The governing body reviews and approves the content of the initial health evaluation and TB screening requirement each year, and records the approval in its minutes.

The offer letter tells the applicant that employment depends on completing the initial health evaluation and TB screening before the first client contact. A form for the health care professional is enclosed.

The new worker has the evaluation done at his or her own provider or the agency's designated clinic, whichever the agency pays for or offers. The agency pays for it as required by law or by [AGENCY NAME]'s benefits policy (PER-09).
The evaluation form is completed and signed by the licensed health care professional, and confirms that the worker has no signs of communicable disease and can perform the job's essential functions.
A TB symptom screen and a TB test are done. Results are written on the form, with the test date and reading date where applicable.

If the TB test is positive or the symptom screen is positive, the worker provides documentation of clinical evaluation (such as a chest X-ray and the clinician's clearance) showing the worker is not infectious before client contact.
A worker with a previously documented positive TB test is not re-tested. The worker provides the prior result and a symptom screen, and gets a clinical evaluation if symptoms are present.

The personnel coordinator reviews the documents for completeness and records only a cleared or not-cleared status on the clearance checklist. Clinical details are kept in the confidential health file.

The health evaluation and TB screening records are kept in a locked, confidential health file that is separate from the personnel file and open only to the Agency Manager, the personnel coordinator when necessary, and IDPH surveyors.
A worker is not scheduled for any client contact until the clearance checklist shows the evaluation and TB screening are complete and cleared.

If a worker is not cleared, the Agency Manager decides on next steps, including a reasonable accommodation or delayed start, without sharing medical details with others. Return to work follows PER-08.
Placed or contracted workers provide proof of an equivalent evaluation and TB screening before starting, and the personnel coordinator files it in the confidential health file (PER-14).
The Agency Manager reviews the clearance log quarterly to confirm that no worker with client contact lacks a completed evaluation and reports to the quality improvement program (GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Sets the health evaluation and TB screening requirements and approves them annually.
Ensures no worker has client contact before clearance and decides on accommodations and uncleared workers.
Sends forms, reviews results, keeps the clearance checklist and secures the confidential health file.
Completes the evaluation and TB screening and signs the form.
Completes the evaluation and screening before first client contact and gives accurate information.

documentation: Governing body minutes approving the health evaluation and TB screening requirements
Completed and signed health evaluation form
TB symptom screen and TB test result, and any follow-up clinical clearance
Clearance checklist (cleared or not cleared only) in the personnel file
Confidential health file stored separately from the personnel file
Quarterly clearance log review

policies.title: Employee Health and Safety Policy — Illness and Exposure Reporting
policies.applies_to: All employees, including the Agency Manager, Alternate Agency Manager, supervisors, schedulers and home services workers, and any contracted worker who has client contact
policies.purpose: To protect clients and employees from communicable and infectious disease and from hazards in the home. The policy requires employees to report symptoms and exposures. It states when an employee is removed from client contact and when the employee may return.
policies.policy:
This policy is [AGENCY NAME]'s employee health and safety policy. It meets 77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.30(c)(1)(H) (employee health policy: reporting of symptoms and exposure to communicable or infectious disease, and removal from and return to client contact). It also meets IDPH Form 445104 item 245.30 c) 1) I) (initial applicants: employee health and safety policy, which 77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.90(a)(3)(I)(ii) ties to both 245.30(c)(1)(H) and (I)).

1. Reporting duty. Every employee must report to the supervisor, before the next client contact, any symptom of a communicable or infectious illness and any exposure to one. Reportable symptoms include fever, new or worsening cough, sore throat, vomiting, diarrhea, undiagnosed rash, jaundice, draining or infected skin lesions, and eye discharge. Reportable exposures include household or close contact with a diagnosed communicable disease, a known or suspected tuberculosis exposure, and a blood or body-fluid exposure on the job.
2. Removal from client contact. An employee with a reportable symptom or exposure is removed from direct client contact until the supervisor has assessed the situation. Where needed, the supervisor gets guidance from the employee's health care provider or the local health department. The supervisor arranges coverage so the client is not left without service (see SVC-09).
3. Return to client contact. Return is allowed only when the criteria in the procedures below are met. The employee is asked for written clearance from a health care provider for tuberculosis, a reportable disease, or any case where the supervisor cannot decide on the facts available. Employees are not required to disclose a diagnosis beyond what is needed to decide on removal and return.
4. No retaliation. No employee is disciplined for reporting an illness or exposure in good faith or for staying home as this policy requires. Leave is handled under PER-09.
5. Infection control. This policy works together with the infection investigation, control and prevention policy required by 77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.75 (SAF-04). The agency follows CDC guidance consistent with that rule.
6. Dangers in the home. Employees must report any hazard to their health or safety found in a client's home, as set out in SAF-06.

definitions.definition: An illness that can be passed from person to person directly or through contact with blood, body fluids, surfaces or the air, such as influenza, COVID-19, norovirus, tuberculosis, scabies and lice.
Close contact with a person who has, or is suspected of having, a communicable disease, or contact with blood or body fluids, in a way that could transmit infection.
Temporary reassignment from, or suspension of, direct in-person contact with clients.
Supervisor approval, supported by written provider or health department clearance when required, that an employee may resume client contact.

procedures: At hire, the Agency Manager gives each employee this policy. The employee signs an acknowledgment that goes in the personnel file (PER-11).
At orientation, the trainer reviews reportable symptoms and exposures, how to report, and the removal and return rules (PER-03). The training is documented under PER-06.

The employee calls the supervisor or the on-call line at [PHONE] before the next scheduled client contact to report any reportable symptom or exposure. Employees must never go to a client's home first and report later.

The supervisor records the report on the Employee Illness/Exposure Report form. The form notes the date, time, symptoms or exposure, last client contact, and the clients seen since the onset of symptoms or the exposure.

The supervisor removes the employee from direct client contact the same day and notifies the scheduler so that visits are covered (SVC-09). The supervisor tells the client or representative if the client may have been exposed.

Fever, cough or other respiratory illness: removal continues until the employee has been fever-free for at least 24 hours without fever-reducing medicine and symptoms are clearly improving. The supervisor may require longer removal or a provider note based on current CDC or local health department guidance.
Vomiting or diarrhea: removal continues until the employee has been symptom-free for at least 48 hours.

Rash, skin infection, scabies, lice or draining lesions: removal continues until a provider has examined the employee and given written clearance, or the lesions are healed or fully covered and not a risk to clients as decided by the supervisor on provider advice.

Suspected or confirmed tuberculosis: the employee is removed immediately and may return only with written clearance from a health care provider or the local health department. The agency follows the screening requirements in PER-07.
Reportable or outbreak-associated disease: the Agency Manager contacts the local health department for guidance on removal, return and notification of affected clients, and follows its instructions.

Household or close-contact exposure: the supervisor decides on the facts and CDC or local health department guidance whether the employee may continue to work, may work with precautions, or must be removed. The decision and reasons are recorded on the report form.

Blood or body-fluid exposure on the job: the employee washes the area right away, reports to the supervisor immediately, and is referred the same day to a health care provider for evaluation. The supervisor completes an incident report under SAF-03.

Return: the employee tells the supervisor before returning. The supervisor confirms the return criteria are met, obtains any required written clearance, and records the return date and approval on the report form.

Dangers in the home: the employee reports to the supervisor, as soon as it is safe to do so, any hazard in a client's home (for example, clients with active illness, unsafe conditions, pests, weapons or violence). The supervisor follows SAF-06 to protect the employee and revise the service plan.
The Agency Manager reviews reports quarterly for patterns and brings findings to the Quality Improvement Program (GOV-04) and the infection control review (SAF-04).
The Agency Manager reviews this policy annually and when CDC or IDPH guidance changes, under GOV-03.

responsibilities.duty: Reports symptoms and exposures before client contact, stays out of client contact when required, and gets clearance before returning.
Receives reports, decides on removal and return, arranges coverage, notifies clients when needed, and documents each case.
Reassigns visits promptly so clients are not left without service.
Maintains this policy, consults the local health department when needed, reviews trends, and ensures there is no retaliation.

documentation: Signed policy acknowledgment (personnel file)
Employee Illness/Exposure Report form, with removal and return dates
Provider or health department clearance notes, kept in the confidential employee health file
Incident reports for on-the-job exposures (SAF-03)
Quarterly summary of reports for the Quality Improvement Program

policies.title: Personnel Policies: Wage Scales, Benefits, Hours and Leave
policies.applies_to: All full-time and part-time employees; the Agency Manager and Administrator administer it
policies.purpose: To state in writing the agency's wage scales, benefits, hours of work and leave so that every employee knows them and the agency applies them consistently.
policies.policy:
This policy meets 77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.30(c)(1)(A) (personnel policies on wage scales, benefits, hours of work and leave time, available to all full- and part-time employees).

1. Availability. [AGENCY NAME] gives these written policies to every full-time and part-time employee at hire. Current copies are kept in the employee handbook, in the office, and with the Agency Manager, who provides them on request.
2. Wage scales. Each position has a written pay range, listed in the Wage Scale Schedule ([WAGE SCALE ATTACHMENT]). No employee is paid less than the minimum wage under the Illinois Minimum Wage Law (820 ILCS 105) or any higher Cook County, Chicago or other local rate that applies where the employee works. The Administrator confirms current state and local rates at least every January 1 and July 1.
3. Benefits. Benefits offered to eligible employees are listed in the Benefits Summary ([BENEFITS SUMMARY ATTACHMENT]), with eligibility rules.
4. Hours of work. Scheduled hours, how work is assigned, meal and rest breaks, paid travel between clients, overtime, and timekeeping follow SVC-10 and PER-15.
5. Leave. The agency provides paid leave under the Illinois Paid Leave for All Workers Act, accruing at no less than 2.5% of hours worked. Where a local ordinance, including Chicago's, gives employees more, the agency applies the more generous rule. Other leave (such as unpaid personal leave, jury duty or family and medical leave, where applicable) is listed in the handbook. Illness leave is applied consistently with the health reporting rules in PER-08, and no employee is penalized for using leave properly.
6. Equal treatment. Wages, benefits and leave are applied without discrimination (CR-05).

definitions.definition: An employee regularly scheduled for [FULL-TIME HOURS] or more hours per week.
An employee regularly scheduled for fewer than [FULL-TIME HOURS] hours per week.
The written pay range for each position, including any differentials.
Paid time away from work that accrues under the Illinois Paid Leave for All Workers Act, or a more generous local ordinance, based on hours worked.

procedures: The Administrator approves and signs the Wage Scale Schedule, Benefits Summary and leave rules before the agency hires its first employee. Each is dated.
At offer stage, the Agency Manager gives the candidate a written offer letter stating position, pay rate, expected hours, pay frequency and benefit eligibility.

At orientation, the Agency Manager gives each new employee a copy of the personnel policies (wages, benefits, hours, leave). The employee signs an acknowledgment and the signed copy goes in the personnel file (PER-11).

The Administrator confirms the state minimum wage and any Cook County or Chicago rate each January 1 and July 1, and before any pay rate change. The confirmation is dated and kept in the compliance binder. Pay rates are raised at once if they fall below the required rate.
The scheduler assigns hours as in SVC-09. The employee reports time worked, including travel time between clients, as in SVC-10. Overtime is handled under PER-15.

Paid leave accrues from the first day of work at a rate not lower than 2.5% of hours worked, as tracked in the payroll system. Each pay statement or online portal shows the accrued and used leave balance.

The employee requests leave from the supervisor as early as possible. Sick leave notice follows PER-08. The supervisor approves leave in writing or electronically and tells the scheduler so that clients' visits are covered.
The Agency Manager records approved leave in the personnel or payroll file.
Before changing any wage scale, benefit or leave term, the Administrator updates the written policy. Employees get at least [NUMBER] days' written notice of changes and sign a new acknowledgment.
Employees may ask the Agency Manager questions about pay, benefits or leave. Questions that remain unresolved go to the Administrator.
The Administrator reviews this policy annually as part of GOV-03 and updates it when state or local law changes.

responsibilities.duty: Approves wage scales, benefits and leave terms; verifies current minimum wage and leave law annually; ensures compliance.
Gives employees the policies, collects acknowledgments, answers questions and keeps records.
Applies hours and leave rules consistently and arranges visit coverage.
Reads the policies, reports time accurately and requests leave according to the policy.

documentation: Signed wage, benefit, hours and leave policy acknowledgments (personnel file)
Wage Scale Schedule and Benefits Summary, dated and approved
Minimum wage and paid leave compliance confirmations
Leave request and approval records, and payroll leave balances
Offer letters

policies.title: Job Descriptions for All Positions
policies.applies_to: All positions used by the agency: Agency Manager, Alternate Agency Manager, Supervisor, Scheduler, and Home Services Worker (caregiver), plus any other position the agency creates
policies.purpose: To define the duties, qualifications, reporting lines and limits of every position so that employees know what is expected and nothing outside the agency's permitted scope is assigned.
policies.policy:
This policy meets 77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.30(c)(1)(D) (job descriptions for all positions used by the agency) and IDPH Form 445104 item 245.30 c) 1 D) (initial applicants: copy of job description for all positions, submitted with the application).

1. A written, dated job description exists for every position the agency uses, before anyone is hired into it.
2. Each description states the position title, to whom it reports, minimum qualifications (including any license, registry or background check requirement), essential duties, physical and working conditions, and limits on duties.
3. The Home Services Worker description matches the permitted scope of non-medical home services in SVC-01 and the task limits in SVC-06 and SVC-07, and expressly excludes nursing tasks. Caregivers do not perform tasks that require a nurse.
4. Descriptions identify essential functions and state that reasonable accommodation is considered for qualified individuals with disabilities, in keeping with the Americans with Disabilities Act (42 USC 12111).
5. Copies of all job descriptions are submitted with the initial IDPH application. Where Form 445104 asks for an Alternate Agency Manager, that position also has a description.

definitions.definition: A written statement of a position's purpose, duties, qualifications, supervision and limits.
The fundamental duties of a position that a person must be able to perform, with or without reasonable accommodation.
An employee who provides non-medical in-home services to clients under the supervision of the agency.

procedures: The Administrator, with the Agency Manager, drafts a job description for each position before the application is submitted: Agency Manager, Alternate Agency Manager, Supervisor, Scheduler, Home Services Worker, and any other position (for example, billing or trainer).

Each description lists title, reporting line, qualifications, essential functions, physical demands, working conditions, hours and any license or registry requirement. Home Services Worker qualifications reflect PER-01, PER-02 and PER-03.

The Agency Manager checks the Home Services Worker description against SVC-01, SVC-06 and SVC-07. The checklist confirms that no nursing tasks are listed and the description states that tasks outside the scope are not to be performed.

The supervisor description includes responsibility for supervisory visits and annual observation (SVC-04 and SVC-05). The Agency Manager and Alternate Agency Manager descriptions include the duties in GOV-01.
The Administrator reviews and signs each description with a date. The Agency Manager files them in the policy manual and keeps a copy with the IDPH application packet.
The agency submits copies of all job descriptions with the initial application (Form 445104).
At offer, the Agency Manager gives the candidate the job description for that position and explains it.
On the first day, the employee signs and dates an acknowledgment that they received and understand the description. The signed copy goes in the personnel file (PER-11).
When duties change or a new position is created, the Agency Manager updates or writes the description before the change takes effect, and the employee signs the revised copy.
The Agency Manager reviews all descriptions annually with PER-12 and GOV-03 and retains the prior versions.
If an employee or applicant asks for an accommodation, the Agency Manager reviews essential functions with the person and any provider information and documents the decision.

responsibilities.duty: Approves all job descriptions and ensures they exist for every position.
Drafts and updates descriptions, checks them against the permitted scope, and obtains employee acknowledgments.
Assigns work consistent with the description and reports when duties go beyond it.
Performs the duties in the job description and does not perform tasks outside it.

documentation: Dated, approved job descriptions for each position
Signed employee acknowledgments (personnel file)
Scope-of-services check for the Home Services Worker description
Copy of job descriptions submitted with the IDPH application
Accommodation request records, if any

policies.title: Personnel Records
policies.applies_to: All employees, including contracted workers where the agency must hold qualification documents; Agency Manager as custodian
policies.purpose: To make sure every employee has a complete, accurate and confidential personnel file that shows the person is qualified and eligible to work and can be produced for an IDPH survey.
policies.policy:
[AGENCY NAME] keeps a personnel file for each employee under 77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.30(c)(2)-(5). Each file contains the employee's name and address, Social Security number, date of birth, next of kin, evidence of qualifications, dates of employment and reason for separation.

For each worker who is not otherwise licensed, certified or registered, the file also holds documentation under 77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.71(a) that there is no disqualifying Health Care Worker Background Check without a waiver, a copy of the Social Security card, and a visa or proof of citizenship that meets federal employment requirements.

Before employing anyone in a position that requires a State professional license, the agency verifies with the Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation (IDFPR) that the license is active and keeps a copy of the verification in the file. For contracted workers who need a license, registration or certification, the agency confirms they hold it and keeps proof (PER-14).

Personnel records are confidential under 77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.30(c)(1)(G). Access is limited to the Administrator, Agency Manager, those who need the file to perform supervisory duties, the employee, and IDPH surveyors or others authorized by law. The Agency Manager is the custodian of personnel files.

Medical and TB screening information (PER-07, PER-08) is kept in a separate confidential employee health file, not in the general personnel file.

definitions.definition: The record of identifying, qualification, eligibility, employment, training and performance documents for one employee.
Documents showing the employee meets the requirements of the position, such as training and competency records, license or certification verification, and references.
The person responsible for maintaining, securing and releasing personnel records.

procedures: The Agency Manager opens a personnel file for each new employee on or before the first day of work, using the Personnel File Checklist.
The employee completes an application and a personal data form giving name, address, date of birth, Social Security number and next of kin. The Agency Manager files them.
The Agency Manager copies the Social Security card and the documents that prove work authorization under federal employment requirements, and files them.

Before any client contact, the Agency Manager files the results of the Health Care Worker Background Check and the IDPH Health Care Worker Registry check, showing no disqualifying result, or a copy of the waiver where one applies (PER-02).

For any position requiring a professional license, the Agency Manager verifies with IDFPR that the license is active before hire. A dated printout of the verification is filed. Licenses are re-verified at renewal.

The Agency Manager files evidence of qualifications: job description acknowledgment (PER-10), orientation and training records (PER-03, PER-06), competency evaluation (PER-04), references, and any certification.
The Agency Manager records the employee's hire date, position and later changes in dates and position.
Annually, the Agency Manager files the annual training record, the registry verification (PER-05), and the performance evaluation (PER-12).

On separation, the Agency Manager records the date and reason for separation (resignation, termination, end of contract, or other) in the file, and keeps the file in the locked, confidential records area.
Files are kept in a locked cabinet or in a password-protected electronic system with access limited to authorized staff. The Agency Manager keeps an access log for requests outside the usual roles.
Medical, TB screening and exposure records go in a separate confidential employee health file.

Quarterly, the Agency Manager audits at least [NUMBER] files, or all files if fewer, against the checklist and records and corrects missing items within 7 days. Findings go to the Quality Improvement Program (GOV-04).
Records are kept for the time stated in the agency retention schedule [RETENTION PERIOD], and are destroyed securely after that time, with a record of destruction.
On request, the Agency Manager makes files available to IDPH surveyors (GOV-06). Release of any other personnel information requires the employee's written consent or a legal requirement.

responsibilities.duty: Custodian of personnel files; creates, audits, secures and releases files.
Ensures required records exist and approves release outside normal access.
Provides accurate documents and keeps address, contact and next-of-kin details current.

documentation: Personnel File Checklist for each employee
Application and personal data form (name, address, SSN, date of birth, next of kin)
Social Security card copy and proof of work authorization
Background check and registry results or waiver
IDFPR license verification (where applicable)
Training, competency and evaluation records
Employment dates and reason for separation
Quarterly file audit results; access log

policies.title: Annual Performance Evaluation
policies.applies_to: All employees, including supervisors and the Agency Manager
policies.purpose: To evaluate each employee's performance at least once a year against the job description, recognize good work, correct problems and identify training needs.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] evaluates the performance of every employee at least once each year, as required by 77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.30(c)(1)(E). Each evaluation is based on the employee's job description (PER-10), direct observation, client and family feedback, attendance, documentation quality and training records. It is combined with the annual observation of home services workers (SVC-05) and the annual training and registry review (PER-05). Evaluations are applied without discrimination (CR-05) and are kept confidential in the personnel file (PER-11).

definitions.definition: A written review, done at least every 12 months, of how well an employee performs the duties in the job description.
The 12 months, counted from the hire date or the last evaluation, covered by the review.
A written plan with specific steps and dates to bring performance up to the expected standard.

procedures: The Agency Manager keeps an evaluation due-date log by employee, based on each hire date, and gives the supervisor the list 30 days before each evaluation is due.

The supervisor gathers input: the job description, the annual observation of the worker (SVC-05), supervisory visit findings (SVC-04), client and family feedback and complaints (CR-02), attendance and punctuality, EVV and visit documentation quality (SVC-10, REC-04), and training completion (PER-05).
The supervisor completes the Annual Performance Evaluation form, rating each job duty and conduct standard (including PER-13) and writing specific examples.

The supervisor confirms with the Agency Manager that annual training hours, the annual registry verification and any license or certification renewals are current. Any gaps are noted on the form with a due date.
The supervisor meets privately with the employee to review the evaluation, discuss strengths and areas for improvement, and set goals and training needs for the coming year.
The employee may add written comments. The employee and the supervisor sign and date the form. The employee's signature shows the review took place, not agreement.

If performance is below expectations, the supervisor writes a corrective action plan with specific steps, support, and a follow-up date no later than 90 days out. The supervisor documents the follow-up.
If a serious concern relates to client safety, abuse, neglect or exploitation, it is handled at once under SAF-01 and SAF-02, not held for the annual evaluation.
The Agency Manager reviews each evaluation for completeness and consistency, then files the original in the personnel file within 14 days of the meeting.
The Agency Manager reports the percentage of evaluations completed on time to the Quality Improvement Program (GOV-04) each quarter. Overdue evaluations are completed within 30 days of the due date.
The Administrator evaluates the Agency Manager and the Alternate Agency Manager annually using the same process.

responsibilities.duty: Prepares and conducts the evaluation, documents observation findings, and follows up on corrective action plans.
Tracks due dates, reviews and files evaluations, and reports completion rates.
Evaluates the Agency Manager and Alternate Agency Manager and ensures the process is followed.
Takes part in the review and carries out the agreed goals and corrective steps.

documentation: Completed, signed Annual Performance Evaluation form (personnel file)
Corrective action plans and follow-up notes
Evaluation due-date log and quarterly completion report
Annual observation record (SVC-05) and training/registry verification records referenced in the evaluation

policies.title: Staff Conduct and Professional Boundaries
policies.applies_to: All employees, volunteers and contracted workers who have contact with clients or their property
policies.purpose: To protect clients from exploitation and misconduct by setting clear standards for conduct and professional boundaries and by making sure suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation is reported.
policies.policy:
[AGENCY NAME] expects every employee to treat clients with dignity and to keep a professional relationship with them at all times.

1. Gifts, loans and money. Employees may not accept gifts, tips, loans, or any money or property from clients or their families, and may not give or lend money to clients. Employees may not borrow from clients or use client property for personal use. Details on gifts and exploitation prevention are in CR-04.
2. Financial dealings. Employees may not handle clients' bank cards, checks, PINs or accounts, except as the service plan allows for an errand with a receipt, and may not enter into personal business, buy or sell items, or become a signer, agent or beneficiary for a client.
3. Exploitative relationships. Employees may not enter a romantic, sexual, or financially or emotionally exploitative relationship with a client, and may not take advantage of a client's dependence.
4. Private arrangements. Employees may not arrange to work privately for a client or the client's family outside the agency while employed with the agency.
5. Confidentiality. Employees keep client and personnel information confidential (CR-03) and do not post about clients, with or without names, on social media.
6. Substances and behavior. Employees must not work under the influence of alcohol or illegal drugs, and must not use threats, harassment, discrimination or abusive language. The agency complies with the Civil Rights Act of 1964 as required by 77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.30(c)(1)(F), and employees must follow CR-05.
7. Mandated reporting. Employees must report any reasonable suspicion of abuse, neglect or financial exploitation of a client to the agency's management and to the elder abuse provider agency designated by IDoA or the Area Agency on Aging, as required by 77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.250 and the Adult Protective Services Act (320 ILCS 20). For a victim under 18, the employee calls the DCFS Child Abuse Hotline. An employee must call 911 or the local police right away for staff-inflicted physical injury, sexual abuse by staff, a crime in the home by another person, or a death other than by disease or natural causes. Reporting duties apply to employees personally and are not removed by telling a supervisor.
8. Alleged perpetrators. An employee who is the alleged perpetrator is removed from direct client contact immediately and the agency investigates (SAF-02).
9. Violations. A violation of this policy may lead to discipline up to termination and, where required, a report to the authorities. No one is retaliated against for a report made in good faith.

definitions.definition: The limit that separates an employee's professional role from personal involvement with a client.
Using a client's money, property or assets improperly or without consent, or by deception or undue influence, for another person's benefit.
A person who must report suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation under the Adult Protective Services Act (320 ILCS 20) and 77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.250.
As used in the Adult Protective Services Act (320 ILCS 20), an adult covered by that Act for the purpose of reporting abuse, neglect or exploitation.

procedures: At hire and orientation, the Agency Manager gives each employee this policy and the abuse reporting steps in SAF-01. The employee signs a conduct and mandated-reporter acknowledgment, filed in the personnel file (PER-11).
The trainer reviews boundaries, gifts, financial dealings, and reporting with every new employee during orientation (PER-03) and again at annual training (PER-05).

If a client offers a gift, tip or loan, the employee politely declines, explains that agency policy does not allow it, and tells the supervisor the same day. The supervisor records the event under CR-04.

If an employee is asked to handle client money, a card or a financial account, the employee declines unless the service plan permits an errand with a written receipt. The employee tells the supervisor of the request.

An employee who becomes aware of a conflict, such as a family relationship with a client or a request to work privately, must report it to the supervisor before accepting any related assignment. The supervisor reassigns the employee as needed.

An employee who suspects abuse, neglect or exploitation, whether by a staff member, family member or anyone else, reports it immediately to the supervisor or Agency Manager at [PHONE] and also to the elder abuse provider agency or Area Agency on Aging (or the DCFS Child Abuse Hotline at [DCFS CHILD ABUSE HOTLINE NUMBER] for a victim under 18), as set out in SAF-01.
If the situation involves staff-inflicted injury, sexual abuse by staff, a crime in the home or an unnatural death, the employee calls 911 first and then reports to the supervisor.
